grounded_facts: Owen Quincy, now hidden in officer's quarters, communicates with Parker York via radio to report encounters.
Owen Quincy informs Parker York about Riley Arden and the Summit Collective, expressing fear and confusion.
memories.memory_text: I was hiding in the officer's quarters when I heard Parker York's voice on the radio, and I immediately told him about Riley Arden and the Summit Collective—I was scared and confused, describing how she almost slit my throat and how those guys looked like a fucked-up gang that was hunting, not a welcoming party.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy concludes that they must attempt to contact the bridge, suspecting other crew members may be awake.
memories.memory_text: I realized we had to try to contact the bridge because I figured we weren't the only ones awake—Team Four wouldn't have gone back to sleep without waking us, so maybe they're on the main deck.

grounded_facts: Parker York communicates his emerging memory about the red key's true purpose to Owen Quincy.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Parker York that this the red key wasn't built to return, and that we're not just transporting cargo — we are the cargo, though he couldn't remember everything.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy has a haunting realization that their mission to Redwood Industries was never intended to return, indicating they are on a one-way settler vessel.
memories.memory_text: I realized we're on a settler's vessel — planetary processing and population, that's what they said. I told myself, Redwood Industries was a one-way ticket all along.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy abruptly asks Parker York about the location of his Jesse Nolan, initiating a line of inquiry about missing spouses.
memories.memory_text: I abruptly asked Parker York where his Jesse Nolan was, needing to know if she was really left behind.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy deduces that the crew's spouses were not left behind but are actually aboard the red key, based on recruitment and breeding tests.
memories.memory_text: I realized we didn't leave our spouses behind — they're on this the red key with us, brought aboard during recruitment and those breeding tests.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy uses the radio to inform Parker York that intruders are on board.
memories.memory_text: I used the radio to tell Parker York that the intruders were on board, saying, 'They're here. Somewhere on board.'

grounded_facts: Parker York interrupts Owen Quincy's emotional outburst and redirects his focus from an immediate, risky rescue attempt to a strategic plan involving the red key control.
memories.memory_text: I was trying to argue that we had to act fast to find the others, but Parker York cut me off and told me to listen — he said going on a wild goose chase wouldn't help and that I needed to focus on the bigger picture.

grounded_facts: Parker York convinces Owen Quincy to prioritize regaining control of the red key over immediately searching for the missing person, reframing the mission to increase overall survival chances.
memories.memory_text: Parker York told me that our main job was to regain control of the red key, and once we had control, finding the missing people would be easier — he said if we saved the red key, we could save them all.

grounded_facts: Parker York instructs Owen Quincy to find the hatch marker over the door to determine their location on the red key.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Parker York to find the hatch marker over the door to figure out where we were on the red key.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy locates and reads a hatch marker to determine his position on the red key, providing critical navigational information.
memories.memory_text: I found the hatch door and climbed up to read the marker—it said D-71643-L—so I called it out to Parker York.

grounded_facts: After failing to use an antique pistol, Owen Quincy discovers and activates an unusual, functional the glass notebook hidden under a desk, significantly enhancing his combat readiness.
memories.memory_text: I tried grabbing a gun from behind glass, but it crumbled in my hand; then I noticed a gap under the desk, reached in, and pulled out an odd-looking the glass notebook that hummed to life when I spun the lever.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy emerges from hiding with determination and begins searching the officer's quarters for tools and weapons, driven by the urgency to find someone before others do.
A focused search operation conducted by Owen Quincy in the officer's living quarters to locate tools, weapons, and navigational clues.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from hiding and immediately began searching the officer's quarters, climbing the angled furniture to look for tools, weapons, and anything that could help me find someone before the others do—I checked the hatch markers to figure out where I was, spotted navigation devices on a mantel, broke the glass to grab a gun, but it crumbled in my hand; then I found a dry flask and finally pulled an unusual the glass notebook from under the desk before heading up through an open hatch.

grounded_facts: Parker York uses the Lakeview House to pull up a diagram of the red key in order to plan a route.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Parker York must have used the Lakeview House to pull up a diagram of the red key, since he started describing a path after working the keyboard and turning up the screen brightness.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy refuses Parker York's suggestion to return to the flight decks, arguing it would be useless since he cannot open the door from his side.
memories.memory_text: I refused Parker York's order to return to the flight decks because I told him it would be useless — I can't open the door from my side.

grounded_facts: Parker York proposes a plan to guide Owen Quincy back toward the flight decks to reunite and find a way to breach the command bridge.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Parker York over the radio that I should head back toward the flight decks to reunite with him and that we'd figure out a way to breach the command bridge together.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy presents a plan to reset the the glass radio despite masking uncertainty, attempting to gain Parker York's cooperation.
Owen Quincy suggests resetting the the glass radio to regain control of the red key, marking a pivotal decision point in the plan to restore functionality.
memories.memory_text: I told Parker York that if he could get me to the Pinecrest Warehouse, I could reset the the glass radio and we could take control of the red key—open the doors, turn on the lights, get to the bridge—and I asked him if he had a better idea.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy interrupts Parker York's instruction to rest, insisting he does not need it and demanding direction.
memories.memory_text: I told Parker York I don't need a rest and demanded to know which way we should go.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy reports reaching the third crossing and provides the marker code to Parker York.
memories.memory_text: I told Parker York I was at the third crossing and gave him the marker code, but he told me to hold up and catch my breath, even though I insisted I didn't need to rest and asked which way to go next.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy arrives at the third Fairview Motel intersection and reports the marker code to Parker York.
memories.memory_text: I reached the third Fairview Motel intersection, checked the marker, and reported the code D-5381-X to Parker York, then I backed against the wall, scanning the Fairview Motel while struggling to catch my breath.

grounded_facts: Due to unease, Owen Quincy slowly backs into a nearby compartment.
memories.memory_text: I felt uneasy because of the shadow movement, so I slowly backed into a nearby compartment for safety.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy notices a shadow moving at the end of the Fairview Motel, causing unease.
memories.memory_text: I noticed a shadow moving at the end of the Fairview Motel while I was scanning, and it made me feel uneasy, so I backed into a nearby compartment.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy discovers a window amidst the wreckage of the infirmary, revealing a view of outer space and an oddly colored moon, which he identifies as Harborview Station.
memories.memory_text: I looked through the wreckage of the infirmary and saw a window with outer space beyond it, and an oddly colored moon—I realized it was Harborview Station.

grounded_facts: Parker York experiences a sudden recollection of the name 'Harborview Station' after hearing it over the radio, indicating a reconnection with a forgotten memory.
memories.memory_text: I said 'The Harborview Station' over the radio, and Parker York suddenly leaned forward, asking what I said—he clearly remembered something when he heard it.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy questions why rotation shifts were shortened and manual override eliminated, implying a cover-up related to Anonymous Screenplay 21.
memories.memory_text: I questioned why the rotation shifts were shortened from three years to two and why the manual override was eliminated, suspecting these changes were hiding something about Anonymous Screenplay 21.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy climbs toward what he believes is a window showing a moon-like view, only to discover it is a reflection created by a light panel and oil on a glass door.
memories.memory_text: I climbed through the debris toward what I thought was a window showing a moon-like view, feeling hopeful as I got closer, only to realize it was just a reflection from a light panel on a glass door smeared with oil — not a real window at all.

grounded_facts: Parker York mutters a cryptic remark suggesting Owen Quincy may have already woken up floating in a coffin, undermining his sense of reality.
memories.memory_text: I heard Parker York mutter 'Who says we didn't?' and it made me wonder if I'd already woken up floating in a coffin—something about it undermined my grip on what's real.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy suggests that the other team may have succumbed to Anonymous Screenplay 21, linking current events to past disaster.
memories.memory_text: I suggested to myself and then out loud that something might have gone wrong with the earlier team—maybe one of them had Anonymous Screenplay 21, just like the officer on Harborview Station. It felt like a real possibility, something we hadn't considered.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy suggests Harborview Station failed due to human error (Anonymous Screenplay 21), challenging Parker York's belief that it was a mechanical failure.
memories.memory_text: I suggested to Parker York that Harborview Station might have failed because of human error—maybe someone suffered from Anonymous Screenplay 21, like cabin fever—and I questioned whether the official story about mechanical failure was really the truth.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy observes his hand trembling, possibly indicating early signs of psychological deterioration or stress.
memories.memory_text: I noticed my hand trembling while holding the the glass notebook, so I made a fist and shook it to steady myself—I couldn't afford to show weakness, not now.

grounded_facts: Parker York instructs Owen Quincy on the route to take through the red key.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Parker York to go left at the third marker and head two more levels down to reach our destination.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy follows Parker York's instructions and moves down the Fairview Motel toward the next location.
memories.memory_text: I followed Parker York's directions and moved down the Fairview Motel toward the next location.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy's voice comes through the radio with concern, prompting Parker York to respond, re-establishing contact.
memories.memory_text: I spoke over the radio, expressing my concern because something didn't feel right, and I knew Parker York would hear me.

grounded_facts: Parker York answers Owen Quincy's uncertain transmission with a direct question, maintaining operational communication.
memories.memory_text: I heard Parker York respond to my transmission with a direct question, keeping our communication focused on the situation.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy finds Riley Foster, a member of Team Six, entangled in a wire snare, initially mistaking him for a previously seen corpse but realizing it's a different, living survivor.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Owen Quincy finds Riley Foster, a member of Team Six, entangled in a wire snare, initially mistaking him for a previously seen corpse but realizing it's a different, living survivor.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy strikes Riley Foster in the gut to stop his screaming, silencing him after he panics upon being discovered.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Owen Quincy strikes Riley Foster in the gut to stop his screaming, silencing him after he panics upon being discovered.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy pulls the wire connected to the hydraulics, causing the snare to snap and freeing Riley Foster, who collapses to the floor gasping.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Owen Quincy pulls the wire connected to the hydraulics, causing the snare to snap and freeing Riley Foster, who collapses to the floor gasping.

grounded_facts: Riley Foster reveals his identity, unit, sector, and belief that Owen Quincy is part of a rescue team.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Riley Foster reveals his identity, unit, sector, and belief that Owen Quincy is part of a rescue team.

grounded_facts: Riley Foster warns Owen Quincy that 'they' are strong, fast, and hunt by scent and sound, advising him to run and not look back.
memories.memory_text: Riley Foster told me they hunt by scent and sound, that they're stronger and faster than expected, and warned me to run and not look back no matter what.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy orders Riley Foster to obey as his commanding officer, citing chain of command.
memories.memory_text: I ordered Riley Foster to wait and obey me as his commanding officer, insisting he follow the chain of command.

grounded_facts: Riley Foster rejects Owen Quincy's authority, stating there is a new CO on board, undermining Owen Quincy's leadership and altering the chain of command perception.
Riley Foster scoffs at Owen Quincy's claim of command, stating there is a new CO on board and dismissing Owen Quincy's authority.
memories.memory_text: I saw the defiance in Riley Foster's eyes when he rejected my authority, scoffing that there's a new CO on board and telling me to fuck off.

grounded_facts: Distant thuds are heard and the glow of blue torches appears at the end of the Fairview Motel, signaling the approach of hostile entities.
memories.memory_text: I heard distant thuds echoing down the Fairview Motel, and then I saw the glow of blue torches growing at the far end, signaling that hostile entities were approaching.

grounded_facts: A tense and traumatic meeting between Owen Quincy and Riley Foster in the Fairview Motel, involving rescue, identification, confrontation, and flight due to approaching threat.
memories.memory_text: I remember that A tense and traumatic meeting between Owen Quincy and Riley Foster in the Fairview Motel, involving rescue, identification, confrontation, and flight due to approaching threat.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy realizes the compartment is separated by thick glass dividers, limiting movement and visibility.
memories.memory_text: I realized the compartment was divided by thick glass barriers when I tried to move forward and bumped into one, limiting where I could go and what I could see.

grounded_facts: Riley Foster silently mouths a command for Owen Quincy not to follow him, expressing anger and refusal to assist.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Foster mouth 'Don't follow me! I can't help you' just before the attack, and I knew he didn't want me to come after him.

grounded_facts: A wire noose snaps around Riley Foster's neck, immobilizing and attacking him; he is subsequently killed by the Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I watched helplessly as a wire noose snapped around Riley Foster's neck and the Summit Collective dragged him away, ending with his neck twisting until it snapped.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy fires at Quinn Hayes, but the energy blast is absorbed by the safety glass divider between them.
memories.memory_text: I fired my the glass notebook at the lead Nico Adler, but the energy blast was absorbed by the glass divider between us.

grounded_facts: The misfired energy blast hits a wall, causing shockwaves that shatter fragile objects and knock over unsecured equipment.
memories.memory_text: I saw the energy blast hit the wall and explode with shockwaves that shattered fragile things and knocked over equipment all around.

grounded_facts: After being fired upon, Quinn Hayes issues a command for the Summit Collective to swarm and pursue Owen Quincy.
memories.memory_text: After I shot at him, I saw Quinn Hayes command the Summit Collective to swarm and pursue me.

grounded_facts: The lead Nico Adler turns to reveal himself as Quinn Hayes, a heavily modified and intimidating figure.
memories.memory_text: I saw the lead Nico Adler turn and reveal himself as Quinn Hayes, a heavily modified and intimidating figure.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy attempts to shoot the lead Nico Adler, but his the glass notebook jams initially and then discharges sideways after manual cranking.
memories.memory_text: I tried to shoot the lead Nico Adler from my hiding spot, but my the glass notebook jammed when I pulled the trigger; I panicked and cranked the energy lever hard, and the gun suddenly blasted sideways with a huge discharge.

grounded_facts: After failing to kill Quinn Hayes and being exposed, Owen Quincy runs to escape the advancing Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I ran for my life after my attack failed and I was exposed, with the Summit Collective advancing on me.

grounded_facts: Parker York shouts into the radio, demanding a response from Owen Quincy in a panicked tone.
Parker York urgently tries to communicate with Owen Quincy via radio after detecting signs of activity or distress.
memories.memory_text: I was told Parker York tried to reach me over the radio, shouting my name in a panicked voice after detecting signs of distress, demanding that I answer him.

grounded_facts: Parker York urgently instructs Owen Quincy not to look back and to keep running through the radio.
memories.memory_text: I heard Parker York's voice over the radio telling me not to look back and to keep running, so I pushed forward even though I was falling apart.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy runs through the Fairview Motel, realizing the Summit Collective have captured and torn apart someone; he is pursued by Summit Collective with inhuman speed.
memories.memory_text: I was running through the Fairview Motel, tripping and bouncing off walls in the dark, and I realized the Summit Collective had just torn someone apart—they're after me now and moving with inhuman speed.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy trips on a wire booby trap, causing him to fall off a loading shaft into an open elevator shaft, but is swung back into a Fairview Motel by a wire around his leg.
memories.memory_text: I was running through the darkness, barely seeing where I was going, and I tripped on a wire that snapped and caught my leg—then I fell into an open elevator shaft, swinging back into a Fairview Motel like a pendulum.

grounded_facts: During the fall, Owen Quincy's transmitter detaches and falls to the bottom of the elevator shaft, exploding on impact.
memories.memory_text: I felt my transmitter break loose as I spun in the air, and I saw it fall all the way to the bottom of the shaft before it exploded on impact.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy attempts to reach the flashlight but fails, pushing it into the loading shaft to avoid detection.
memories.memory_text: I was hanging upside down and saw the glow of torches in the loading shaft, so I tried to reach the flashlight but couldn't grab it, and instead I pushed it into the shaft to keep it from giving me away.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy is violently pulled upward by the cable after being caught in it, narrowly avoiding the approaching figure.
memories.memory_text: I was violently jerked upward by the cable, spinning wildly as it pulled me away from the wall and slammed me into the ceiling before swinging me toward the open shaft.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison slashes the wire binding Owen Quincy, allowing him to fall to the floor and escape imminent danger.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Ellison slash the wire that was binding me, and I broke free, falling to the floor just as the cable was yanked up and out of sight.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison examines Owen Quincy's uniform and tattoo, then shows his own to confirm shared affiliation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Ellison jab at the emblems on my uniform and tap my tattoo, then show me his own emblem and tattoo, confirming we were on the same side.

grounded_facts: After verifying Owen Quincy's identity, Drew Ellison returns his energy gun and gives him a flashlight, signaling alliance.
memories.memory_text: After verifying who I was, Drew Ellison handed back my energy gun and gave me a flashlight, signaling that he was on my side.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy communicates his intent to investigate the red key's malfunction by going to the the glass radio.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Ellison I was going to the the glass radio to try to fix what went wrong with the red key.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy tries to convince Drew Ellison to remain in place for safety, but Drew Ellison does not comply.
memories.memory_text: I told Drew Ellison to stay behind for safety, but when I looked back, he was gone—though I later realized he must have followed me anyway.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy enters a recreational room with pool tables, video games, and a ransacked bar, indicating possible prior human activity and resource depletion.
memories.memory_text: I entered the rec room and saw pool tables, video games, and a ransacked bar, so I wiped a wet spot on the bar and tasted it to figure out what it was.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden lunges from a cabinet and physically assaults Owen Quincy, initiating combat by striking him and attempting to stab him.
Riley Arden violently attacks Owen Quincy by lunging from hiding and attempting to stab him.
memories.memory_text: I was struck hard under the jaw and thrown backward over a table when someone lunged from a cabinet; I saw it was Riley Arden as she jumped on me and tried to stab me in the neck.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison saves Owen Quincy by striking Riley Arden and interrupting her attack.
Drew Ellison intervenes in the fight by striking Riley Arden, saving Owen Quincy from being killed.
memories.memory_text: I was pinned down and about to be stabbed in the neck when Drew Ellison lunged in, striking Riley Arden and knocking her away, saving my life.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy uses a warning shot and verbal command to stop the fight between Riley Arden and Drew Ellison.
Owen Quincy fires a deliberate warning shot to stop the conflict between Drew Ellison and Riley Arden.
memories.memory_text: I fired a warning shot past Riley Arden and shouted 'Hold it!' and then 'Knock it off! Both of ya!' to stop her and Drew Ellison from fighting.

grounded_facts: A violent encounter and subsequent de-escalation involving Owen Quincy, Drew Ellison, and Riley Arden in a recreational room.
memories.memory_text: I was knocked back and nearly stabbed in the neck by Riley Arden, but Drew Ellison hit her and saved me; after she attacked him with a pool ball and I blinded her with my flashlight, I fired a warning shot past her to stop the fight and told both of them to knock it off before we all backed away from the confrontation.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison gestures to her uniform emblem and grins, indicating mutual understanding and willingness to cooperate.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Ellison gesture to the emblem on my uniform and then grin, showing me she understood and was willing to cooperate.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy advocates for collaboration among the three characters to increase chances of survival and escape.
Owen Quincy suggests that they work together for mutual survival and escape.
memories.memory_text: I told the others we should work together because we all want the same thing, and as long as we understand each other, we can survive and escape.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy demands to know who Riley Arden is after she interrupts them, seeking to establish her role and threat level.
memories.memory_text: I stopped her and demanded to know who she was, making it clear she couldn't just join us without a name.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden informs Owen Quincy and Drew Ellison that they are heading in the wrong direction toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, providing critical navigational information.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riley Arden that we were heading in the wrong direction toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, and she refused to go back down that way because no one ever comes back.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy physically grabs Riley Arden's arm to stop her from leaving, leading to a moment of tension and resistance.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed her arm to stop her from leaving, and she yanked away, ready to fight me.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden tests Owen Quincy's competence by asking if he can actually fly the red key, assessing his usefulness and credibility.
memories.memory_text: She questioned whether I could fly the red key, asking me twice if I could handle it if I had to.

grounded_facts: An unplanned meeting in the Fairview Motel between Owen Quincy, Drew Ellison, and Riley Arden that results in critical information exchange and a temporary coordination of movement.
memories.memory_text: I was moving down the Fairview Motel with Drew Ellison, trying to force open a sealed door, when I saw Riley Arden appear behind us; we turned back with weapons ready, and after a tense exchange where she questioned who we were and where we were going, I told her I needed her to show me the way, and though she warned me about the the glass radio path being dangerous, I saw her start moving up the Fairview Motel and I followed with Drew Ellison.

grounded_facts: After being questioned and challenged, Riley Arden agrees to lead Owen Quincy toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, though she refuses to wait for him.
memories.memory_text: I got her to agree to lead me toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, but she made it clear she wouldn't wait for me.

grounded_facts: Bolter asks Riley Arden if she knows where she is going and expresses discomfort with the environment.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bolter ask Riley Arden if she knew where she was going, and he said the environment didn't feel right.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden sharply tells Owen Quincy to be quiet, warning that his loud voice could get them killed.
memories.memory_text: Riley Arden sharply told me to be quiet, warning that my loud voice could get us killed.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy expresses shock and disbelief upon hearing that people have been awake for months.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't believe it when I heard people had been awake for months, and I shouted, 'How could you have—people running around on board for several months!?'

grounded_facts: Riley Arden discloses that she has been awake for two to three months, indicating she was not the first to awaken.
memories.memory_text: Riley Arden told me she's been awake for two to three months and that she wasn't the first one to wake up.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden leads Owen Quincy and Drew Ellison through a large atrium with multiple shafts, moving toward a side shaft.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden lead me and Drew Ellison through a large atrium filled with shafts, and she guided us toward a side shaft.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden silences Owen Quincy twice to prevent noise that might alert the Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I asked Riley Arden where we were going and what we were doing, but she silenced me twice—first with a sharp 'Shush!' and then a firm 'Quiet!'—so I knew I had to stay silent to avoid alerting the Summit Collective.

grounded_facts: The group observes a bluish glow and moving shadows indicating the approach of Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I saw a bluish glow growing stronger at the end of the Fairview Motel, and shadows moving closer, so I knew the Summit Collective were approaching.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy physically stops Drew Ellison from fleeing as the Summit Collective approach.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Drew Ellison's shoulder to stop him from fleeing when he tried to leave as the Summit Collective approached.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy notices Riley Arden's ID tattoo: BIO-T>>218>>076, revealing her affiliation or identity.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Riley Arden's ID tattoo—BIO-T>>218>>076—when the control panel activated, and it made me wonder about her connection to a bio-lab.

grounded_facts: The group squeezes through the partially open vault door and manually pushes it shut, sealing themselves inside.
memories.memory_text: I squeezed through the half-open vault door with the others and helped push it shut, sealing us inside with a loud clank.

grounded_facts: The group arrives at the steel vault door and takes cover, initiating a waiting phase under Riley Arden's direction.
A tense confrontation at the bio-lab vault door as the group evades approaching Summit Collective and attempts to gain entry.
memories.memory_text: I remember arriving at the steel vault door with the group, crouching in the shadows under Riley Arden's direction as she gestured for us to stay put; I didn't know what we were waiting for at first, but then I saw the bluish glow growing stronger down the Fairview Motel and heard the hiss and cackles of the Summit Collective approaching, making me grip my the glass notebook tighter while watching Riley Arden for cues.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden attempts to open the vault door using a hand scanner, but the power surge cuts out, leaving the door only partially open.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden try to open the vault door with a hand scanner during a power surge, but the power cut out before it fully opened, leaving just enough space for us to squeeze through.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden locks the door and jams it with a pipe to prevent entry, adding her own security measure.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden secure the door and jam it with a pipe to make sure nothing could get in.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy observes the rows of labeled glass tubes containing biological specimens for repopulation on Tanis.
memories.memory_text: I was in awe as I approached the wall of glass tubes, seeing rows of labeled containers glistening with condensation, clearly holding biological specimens meant for repopulation on Tanis.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden informs Owen Quincy that the vault contains embryos for repopulating livestock and wildlife on Tanis.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riley Arden that the vault contains embryos for repopulating livestock and wildlife on Tanis as part of the Ecological Development, Embryonic Charter.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy remembers that the journey to Tanis was a 123-year flight, realizing the implications of their extended hibernation.
memories.memory_text: I realized I hadn't remembered just how far away Tanis was until I recalled that our flight was supposed to last 123 years.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden responds to Owen Quincy's surprise about forgetting the flight duration by explaining fragmented memory recovery.
Riley Arden explains that memories return only in fragments despite months awake, including loss of personal identity but retention of technical training.
memories.memory_text: I was surprised I couldn't remember the flight duration, and Riley Arden told me that memories only come back in fragments—even after months awake—and that technical training returns first, while personal memories like where she grew up or her brother's name are still missing.

grounded_facts: A meeting in the bio-lab vault where Owen Quincy learns about the ecological mission, memory loss, and possible oversleeping.
memories.memory_text: I was in awe looking at the wall of glass tubes, and I noticed how carefully Riley Arden checked the systems; she told me that her memories only come in pieces, even after months, and that the training comes back first—something I started to believe as I tried to make sense of my own gaps.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden suggests they have been asleep longer than assumed, based on degradation of systems and food.
Riley Arden uses the state of dehydrated food and the red key systems to suggest they have been asleep far longer than believed.
memories.memory_text: Riley Arden told me she thinks we've been asleep longer than I believe, based on how long it takes for coal to turn into diamonds and how the red key's systems are degrading beyond what would happen in just a few years.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden gathers tools and supplies, slinging a bag over her shoulder, indicating readiness to depart the bio-lab vault.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden gathering tools and supplies, and when she slung the bag over her shoulder, I knew she was ready to go.

grounded_facts: The hatch to the ventilation shaft is broken open, allowing access.
The passage inside the ventilation shaft is blocked by a wall collapse, preventing further travel.
memories.memory_text: I broke open the hatch and shone my flashlight into the ventilation shaft, seeing that the passage was blocked twenty feet in by a wall collapse.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden communicates the existence of another, less safe way through the shaft.
Riley Arden reveals knowledge of another, less safe way through, introducing a new travel option.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riley Arden that there's another way through, though it's less safe, and that this is the only other option she knows of.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden dismisses Owen Quincy's attempt to search for his Jesse Nolan by informing him that family members are not housed in this section.
memories.memory_text: I told Riley Arden my Jesse Nolan was brought with us, even though she wasn't crew, and she told me that meant my Jesse Nolan wasn't in this section because only development settlers and engineers were housed here.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden repeatedly orders Owen Quincy to stay quiet and keep moving, asserting control over the situation due to perceived danger.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden repeatedly telling me to keep quiet and keep moving, insisting we couldn't stay out in the open because of the danger.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy calls out to Drew Ellison to rejoin the group as they prepare to leave the area.
memories.memory_text: I called out to Drew Ellison, telling him to come on and let's get out of there as we were preparing to leave.

grounded_facts: The group enters the Lakeview House to investigate the status of the crew and navigate through the damaged facility.
Owen Quincy realizes that the Lakeview House in the Lakeview House hyper-sleep compartment are all empty, leading to concern about the missing crew.
memories.memory_text: I entered the Lakeview House with the group and saw that all the pods were open and empty — my God, I remember saying it out loud — and I couldn't stop myself from asking where everyone had gone. I started wondering if my Jesse Nolan might be among them, even though she wasn't part of the crew, and I began looking for her name on the chambers while also trying to figure out where the family members could be.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy stops moving and focuses on checking the nameplates of the Lakeview House, hoping to find his Jesse Nolan among the settlers.
memories.memory_text: I stopped moving and turned to check the nameplates on the Lakeview House, hoping to find my Jesse Nolan among the settlers, even though I had to leave Drew Ellison behind.

grounded_facts: The group abandons Drew Ellison as he remains fixated on a distant threat, while Owen Quincy follows Riley Arden away, leaving Drew Ellison behind.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Ellison crouched and fixated on something in the dark, refusing to move, so I hesitated but then followed Riley Arden away, leaving him behind.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden dismisses Owen Quincy's plea to wait for Drew Ellison, asserting her intent to leave without him.
memories.memory_text: I pleaded with Riley Arden to wait for Drew Ellison, but she told me to wait and find my own way, making it clear she was leaving without him.

grounded_facts: Faced with the choice of waiting for Drew Ellison or following Riley Arden, Owen Quincy chooses to chase after her.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated when Riley Arden ran ahead, torn between waiting for Drew Ellison and following her, but I chose to chase after her.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden realize they have entered a chamber filled with stacked human skeletons and carcasses.
memories.memory_text: I realized Riley Arden and I had crawled into a pit filled with stacked skeletons and carcasses, and horror hit me as we saw remains all around us.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden grabs Owen Quincy to stop him from speaking when a Nico Adler is nearby.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden suddenly grabbing me to silence me just as a shadow passed with a cackling hiss—I could feel the bones crinkling beneath us as we froze in place.

grounded_facts: A Nico Adler appears and attacks Owen Quincy and Riley Arden, leading to a violent confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Nico Adler vanish after we slid down the slope, but then it lunged at us—I was struck so hard I flew into a pile of bones, and I remember charging back into it, fighting alongside Riley Arden and Drew Ellison under flickering light until we brought it down.

grounded_facts: Quinn Hayes taps his spear to signal the Summit Collective, creating a threatening display.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Hayes slowly tap his spear against the wall, the clanking echoing through the hull, and I knew it was a threat — a signal to the Summit Collective.

grounded_facts: Quinn Hayes taps his spear, signaling other Summit Collective and causing the room to fill with them.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Hayes start tapping his spear against the wall, and I realized right away that the sound was summoning more Summit Collective—the room began to fill with them.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison emerges from the shadows and attacks the Nico Adler, turning the tide of the battle.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Ellison burst from the shadows and strike the Nico Adler with his pipe, which gave us the opening we needed to fight back.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy argues that Drew Ellison saved his life and should not be abandoned.
memories.memory_text: I argued that Drew Ellison saved my life twice and I wasn't going to leave him behind, even as the walls came alive and Summit Collective swarmed toward us.

grounded_facts: After defeating one Nico Adler and seeing more arrive, the group decides to run.
memories.memory_text: After I helped take down one of those Summit Collective with Riley Arden and Drew Ellison, I saw more shadows moving in — the room was filling with them. I realized we were being overwhelmed, and when Riley Arden shouted 'Run!', I didn't hesitate. I followed her and Drew Ellison as we fled, the walls coming alive with Summit Collective swarming toward us like wild dogs.

grounded_facts: A tense and horrifying confrontation in a chamber filled with human remains, where the group faces a Nico Adler and is subsequently ambushed by more.
memories.memory_text: I crawled with Riley Arden into a dark chamber filled with human remains, and we froze when a Nico Adler passed by with a hiss; I felt the bones shift under us before we slid down into a fight where the Nico Adler attacked us, I was thrown into a pile of bones, and then Drew Ellison joined in—we barely brought it down together, only to realize more Summit Collective were swarming toward us.

grounded_facts: After the group escapes, Quinn Hayes and his pack pause to eat the defeated Nico Adler.
memories.memory_text: I looked back as we were escaping and saw Quinn Hayes and his pack stop to eat the fallen Nico Adler.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy, unable to find his own chamber, dives into the same chamber as Riley Arden and closes the hatch.
memories.memory_text: I dove into the chamber with Riley Arden and pulled the hatch shut because I couldn't find an open one of my own.

grounded_facts: Summit Collective move past the porthole in a search-and-destroy manner, creating intense fear in Owen Quincy and Riley Arden who remain hidden and motionless.
memories.memory_text: I was crammed against Riley Arden, both of us gasping and drenched in sweat as I saw the silhouettes of Summit Collective moving past the porthole with weapons, searching; when one stepped close, I froze and held my breath, terrified they'd see us, until their shadows finally faded away.

grounded_facts: After the Summit Collective pass, Owen Quincy reacts with shock and fear, questioning what happened to the Summit Collective and what they have become.
memories.memory_text: I reacted with shock and fear after the Summit Collective passed, yelling out loud about what they've become because I couldn't make sense of it.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden tells Owen Quincy to shut up after he speaks out loud, likely to prevent detection by the Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riley Arden to shut up right after I spoke, probably because she feared the Summit Collective would hear me.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden crawl out of the hatch door into the main Fairview Motel, joining Drew Ellison who is already waiting.
memories.memory_text: I peeked out of the hatch and then crawled out with Riley Arden into the main Fairview Motel, where Drew Ellison was already waiting for us.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy urges immediate action to flee, while Riley Arden suggests returning to find another path, leading to tension.
memories.memory_text: I urged everyone to just go and get out of there right away, but Riley Arden wanted to go back and find another path, which made me frustrated because I knew there wasn't one, and we started arguing about which way to go while Drew Ellison stood by.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy attempts to stand and help the Big Passenger, but Riley Arden pulls him back to prevent detection.
memories.memory_text: I tried to stand up to help the Big Passenger, but Riley Arden pulled me back, and I remember yelling that we had to help him before it was too late.

grounded_facts: As Owen Quincy attempts to intervene during the Summit Collective' attack, Drew Ellison forcibly grabs and holds him back.
memories.memory_text: I broke free from Riley Arden and moved to intervene, but Drew Ellison grabbed me hard and held me back, stopping me from reaching the Big Passenger.

grounded_facts: The Summit Collective gather in a circle around the wounded Big Passenger, perform a ceremonial prayer, and then consume him in a frenzied, ritualistic manner.
memories.memory_text: I watched in horror as the Summit Collective surrounded the wounded Big Passenger, performed a ceremonial prayer, and then attacked and consumed him in a frenzied ritual while Harper Foster led them in a twisted dance under the flickering lights.

grounded_facts: A power surge causes flickering lights and activates a blinking light on a sleep-chamber; shortly after, the hatch is violently kicked open with white gas escaping.
memories.memory_text: I saw the lights flicker from a power surge, and then the hatch was kicked open with white gas escaping, so I crawled with the others into the shadows to hide.

grounded_facts: A Big Passenger crawls out of the hatch, struggling physically, then is struck by Quinn Hayes and captured by the Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I watched a Big Passenger crawl out of the hatch, struggling and gasping, then get struck by Quinn Hayes and captured by the Summit Collective, and I was frozen in horror until Drew Ellison pulled me toward a floor grate to escape.

grounded_facts: The Summit Collective gather around the wounded Big Passenger, perform a ceremonial ritual, and then brutally attack and eat him alive.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Summit Collective return and knock down the Big Passenger who had just crawled out of the hatch, and I watched in horror as they formed a circle, said some kind of prayer over him, and then tore into him with their weapons and began eating him alive while Harper Foster led them in a wild dance.

grounded_facts: After witnessing the attack, Owen Quincy, Riley Arden, and Drew Ellison retreat to a corner where Riley Arden lifts a floor grate; they climb into a dark shaft to escape.
memories.memory_text: I was frozen in horror, then felt Drew Ellison pull me along as I followed Riley Arden to a corner where she lifted a floor grate; we climbed into a dark shaft to get away.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy challenges Riley Arden's leadership and decision-making during their escape attempt.
memories.memory_text: I directly challenged Riley Arden's leadership, calling out that we were doing laps down here and that she should've been more honest about the plan.

grounded_facts: Tension rises between Owen Quincy and Riley Arden over the purpose and direction of their journey, revealing distrust.
memories.memory_text: I questioned Riley Arden's direction when I realized we were going in circles, and the tension between us escalated as she defended her choices, insisting she was trying to save us all.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden justifies her involvement by emphasizing her role in saving Owen Quincy.
memories.memory_text: I was told Riley Arden didn't need to help me at all, and that she saved us from staying stuck on level eight.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison halts the argument between Owen Quincy and Riley Arden by drawing attention to an external sound.
memories.memory_text: I was arguing with Riley Arden when Drew Ellison hissed for us to be quiet and listen, and then I heard classical music echoing from below.

grounded_facts: A group effort to navigate and escape from a confined, industrial sub-level environment.
memories.memory_text: I remember crawling through a tight steel passageway with Drew Ellison and Riley Arden, all of us working together to navigate our way out of the sub-level, even as doubts grew.

grounded_facts: The group discovers a concealed, habitable area inside a storage tank, suggesting prior human activity and survival efforts.
memories.memory_text: I heard classical music echoing from below and followed the sound with Drew Ellison and Riley Arden, reaching an open hatch where we saw a hidden living space inside a storage tank—chairs around a makeshift table with candles and food containers—and I began climbing through with Drew Ellison while Riley Arden hesitated.

grounded_facts: A stream of colorless chemical gas is released into the tank, causing the characters to choke.
memories.memory_text: I felt the colorless gas hit us and started choking as it filled the tank.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter shouts at Drew Ellison to stop climbing and return, attempting to prevent his ascent.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter shout at Drew Ellison to stop climbing and get back down.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison attempts to climb the slanted wall and reach the catwalk but is forced to let go after being jabbed by Jesse Colter with a spear.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Ellison try to climb the wall and grab the pipe, but then Jesse Colter jabbed his hand with a spear and he fell back down.

grounded_facts: The hatch to the tank closes suddenly due to a triggered trap, trapping Drew Ellison, Riley Arden, and Owen Quincy inside.
memories.memory_text: I saw the hatch slam shut right after Riley Arden stepped through—it was some kind of trap with a snapping wire and clanking levers, and then the whole tank jolted when the energy blast hit, sending sparks flying into the gas.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy fires an the glass notebook at the hatch, creating a spark that ignites the chemical gas.
The chemical gas is ignited by the energy blast, causing a burst of flame that rolls into the catwalks and knocks Jesse Colter off his feet.
memories.memory_text: I fired my the glass notebook at the hatch, creating a spark that ignited the chemical gas—I saw the burst of flame roll into the catwalks and knock Jesse Colter off his feet.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy points his the glass notebook at Jesse Colter and demands he shut off the gas.
memories.memory_text: I pointed my the glass notebook at Jesse Colter and shouted at him to shut off the gas, angling the barrel toward the vent to make him understand the danger.

grounded_facts: Under threat from Owen Quincy, Jesse Colter shuts off the flow of chemical gas by manipulating levers and nozzles.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter scramble across the catwalk and manipulate the levers and nozzles to shut off the gas flow after I forced him to do it.

grounded_facts: After shutting off the gas, Jesse Colter reacts with curiosity and offers to trade for the the glass notebook.
Jesse Colter, after seeing the the glass notebook's power, suggests trading for it.
Jesse Colter expresses surprise and asks Owen Quincy where he got the the glass notebook.
memories.memory_text: After I shut off the gas, Jesse Colter first asked me where I got the the glass notebook, then shifted from fear to curiosity, staring at the barrel before asking if I was looking to trade.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter cranks an energy lever to turn on auxiliary lights, expanding visibility in the water processor room.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter crank an energy lever that turned on a string of auxiliary lights, which suddenly widened my view of the water processor room.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter reports that the captain is dead, with body parts scattered across different decks.
memories.memory_text: I was told the captain is dead, with pieces scattered across B-Deck, C-Deck, the promenade, and even his nuts in the foosball game in the rec room.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy asks Jesse Colter to come down to meet properly, but Jesse Colter refuses due to fear of contamination.
memories.memory_text: I asked Jesse Colter to come down so we could meet properly, but he refused, saying he was too sensitive to the dust bug and didn't know where we'd been.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter lowers a bin of food via wire for the group, claiming it is kosher.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter lower a bin of food down to us on a wire, and he claimed it was kosher before we could even check it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter greets and interacts with Owen Quincy, Riley Arden, and Drew Ellison in the water processor, offering food and information.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Jesse Colter greeted me, Riley Arden, and Drew Ellison, telling us to make ourselves at home and not to pet the rat, and later mentioned the food was Kosher.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy asks Jesse Colter about the Pinecrest Warehouse, confirming Jesse Colter has knowledge of the red key layout.
memories.memory_text: I asked Jesse Colter if he knew where the Pinecrest Warehouse was, trying to confirm whether he had knowledge of the red key's layout.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter implies Owen Quincy has just woken up, suggesting knowledge about the group's state.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter say I just woke up, implying that I didn't realize it myself.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter cooks a makeshift soup using powder and heated water, treating the act with exaggerated care and humor.
memories.memory_text: I watched Jesse Colter carefully stir some powder into heated water, making a big show of it like he was preparing a gourmet meal.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter admits he has lost track of time, referencing having stopped counting after a band broke up decades ago, and comments on time distortion in the red key.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter say he had stopped counting time after a band broke up decades ago, and I realized how distorted our sense of time has become.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter makes a sarcastic comment about writing a complaint to the airline, reflecting disillusionment and coping through irony.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Colter saying he was going to write a strongly worded letter to the airline, and I knew he was being sarcastic about our situation.

grounded_facts: An informal gathering where Jesse Colter distributes soup to the group, attempting to create a moment of normalcy and connection.
Jesse Colter lowers bowls of soup to the others, framing it as a festive ritual.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter lower bowls of soup down to us in the bin, making it feel like some kind of ritual, and I understood he was trying to create a moment of normalcy for all of us.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy speculates whether the creatures came from Jesse Colter's lab or boarded the red key, prompting Riley Arden's theory.
memories.memory_text: I wondered if those creatures came from Jesse Colter's lab or if something had boarded the red key during hibernation, so I asked Riley Arden about it.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden suggests that the creatures may have originated from the synthetic enzyme 'accelerator' in the feeding tubes, which was meant to help humans adapt to Tanis but instead caused the creatures to adapt to the red key environment.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riley Arden that the creatures might have come from the synthetic enzyme 'accelerator' in the feeding tubes, which was meant to help us adapt to Tanis but instead caused them to adapt to the red key environment.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy asks Jesse Colter to explain the content of the distorted message.
memories.memory_text: I asked Jesse Colter what that distorted message was saying because I couldn't make out the words myself.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter adjusts the playback speed of the recording, making its content gradually intelligible.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter adjust the playback speed, cranking the lever and whispering along until his voice matched the recording.

grounded_facts: The group hears the final message from humanity: they are the last survivors, blessed and sent forward by those who came before.
memories.memory_text: I heard the message become clear at last—Jesse Colter spoke in unison with the recording, and I realized we were all that remained of humanity, blessed and sent forward by those who came before us.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter actively plays and interprets the recording for Owen Quincy and Riley Arden, inviting them into a moment of shared meaning.
A moment in which Jesse Colter shares and deciphers the final recorded message from Earth, drawing Owen Quincy and Riley Arden into a shared experience of revelation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter play the recording with excitement, dancing as he repeated it, and I could feel the weight of the moment as Riley Arden and I moved closer, drawn into this shared experience of trying to grasp what it meant.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter plays a heavily distorted recording from a makeshift device, revealing a message from Earth's past.
memories.memory_text: I heard the distorted message from Earth coming through the makeshift device, barely understandable, and I realized how fragile and faint our connection to the past had become.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy abruptly stops Jesse Colter mid-narrative, demanding to hear the transmission again, expressing disbelief.
memories.memory_text: I interrupted Jesse Colter mid-story, shouting 'HOLD IT!' and demanding he play the transmission again because I couldn't believe what I was hearing.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden leans toward Owen Quincy and questions whether Jesse Colter's story could be true, seeking reassurance or shared interpretation.
memories.memory_text: Riley Arden leaned toward me, asking if Jesse Colter's story could be real, and I told her I didn't know—it just couldn't be true, but I wasn't sure.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter narrates the story of the lone pilot who turned into a tyrannical 'King' by torturing and devouring passengers, then exiling the obedient survivors into cargo holds.
memories.memory_text: I was told the story of the lone pilot who became a tyrannical 'King'—how he tortured and devoured passengers in their sleep and later exiled the obedient survivors into the cargo holds.

grounded_facts: A dramatic, staged narration by Jesse Colter using wall drawings to depict the red key's dark history and Owen Quincy's prophesied role.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Jesse Colter's dramatic narration using wall drawings to depict the red key's dark history, and I remember him sketching my own journey toward the the glass radio as part of the story.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter shifts the narrative to include Owen Quincy as a 'gallant knight' destined to awaken the the glass radio and lead the red key to salvation.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Colter shifting the story to include me as a gallant knight destined to wake the the glass radio and lead the red key to salvation, sketching my journey toward the core while proclaiming me the new king who would light the torch and bring us to paradise.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden, upon waking, accuses Jesse Colter of trying to eat her and threatens him with a the glass notebook.
Riley Arden wakes up to find Jesse Colter kneeling over her and accuses him of attempting to eat her, leading to a confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riley Arden that Jesse Colter was going to eat her and that he had gassed them all, after she woke up and found him kneeling over her.

grounded_facts: The water processor shudders violently, signaling that the the glass radio has entered its final phase before shutdown.
memories.memory_text: I felt the water processor shudder and confirmed the the glass radio had begun its final phase before shutdown.

grounded_facts: A critical group confrontation occurs inside the water processor as the the glass radio enters its final cycle and morale collapses.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the shudder shake the tank as we watched the ceiling, and I realized the the glass radio had gone into its final cycle, with Riley Arden shouting that we were meant to go on and that we're the last.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy admits defeat, declaring that the mission is over and there is no reason to continue.
memories.memory_text: I saw the the glass radio enter the final cycle and knew we had no time left—I told Jesse Colter it was over, that there was no Earth to return to and nothing left worth saving.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden confronts Owen Quincy, insisting that their duty and purpose remain despite the odds.
Riley Arden physically grabs Owen Quincy and demands he not give up, challenging his despair.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden grabbing me, her eyes blazing as she shouted, 'Don't give up on me!'—she insisted we still had a duty to go on, even after everything was lost.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter's the red box crackles back to life, indicating returning power and potential communication capability.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter's the red box crackle back to life, so I knew the power was returning and we might be able to communicate again.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy urgently asks Jesse Colter if he has a radio, then demands an answer.
memories.memory_text: I urgently asked Jesse Colter if he had a radio, then demanded to know—my voice was loud, desperate—because I needed to find a way to reach someone.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy initiates a radio call to check if Parker York can hear him, marking the start of renewed contact.
memories.memory_text: I reached out over the radio to check if Parker York could hear me, hoping to reestablish contact after the silence.

grounded_facts: Parker York reestablishes radio communication with Owen Quincy after a period of silence or disconnection.
memories.memory_text: I called out to Parker York over the radio, hoping he could hear me, and then I heard his voice respond—he was back online.

grounded_facts: Parker York answers Owen Quincy's radio call, confirming he is alive and responsive.
memories.memory_text: I heard Parker York respond to my radio call, confirming he was alive and able to answer.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy uses the radio to convey the severity of the the glass radio's condition, emphasizing the red key's imminent permanent shutdown.
memories.memory_text: I used the radio to tell Parker York the red key's the glass radio was failing and that we were facing permanent shutdown—I made it clear there would be no return and that we needed to reset it.

grounded_facts: Parker York and Spencer Huxley exchange a prolonged silent stare, reflecting unspoken tension or uncertainty.
memories.memory_text: I saw Parker York and Spencer Huxley share a silent stare, their tension hanging in the air without a word.

grounded_facts: Parker York acknowledges Owen Quincy's message and agrees on the necessity to reset the red key's system to prevent permanent shutdown.
memories.memory_text: I heard Parker York acknowledge my message and say, 'I hear you. How do we get you in there?'

grounded_facts: Parker York acknowledges Owen Quincy's message and asks how to facilitate his entry, showing cooperation under pressure.
memories.memory_text: I heard Parker York acknowledge my message and ask how to get me in, showing he was ready to help despite the pressure.

grounded_facts: A critical radio exchange between Owen Quincy and Parker York regarding the red key's failing the glass radio and impending shutdown.
memories.memory_text: I had a critical radio exchange with Parker York about the red key's failing the glass radio and the impending permanent shutdown, where I conveyed the urgency and he responded with a plan to get me access.

grounded_facts: Parker York begins typing on the Lakeview House to generate a path for Owen Quincy, indicating active response to the crisis.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Parker York began typing on the Lakeview House to generate a path for me, responding to the crisis after our exchange.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison shakes his head and gestures to stop Owen Quincy from entering the hatchway, conveying caution non-verbally.
Drew Ellison physically stops Owen Quincy from entering through the hatchway, indicating danger or caution.
memories.memory_text: I was about to step through the hatchway when Drew Ellison grabbed me and pulled me back, shaking his head to stop me, making it clear I shouldn't go in.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter asks Owen Quincy to translate what Drew Ellison said in Japanese.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Colter asked me to translate what Drew Ellison said in Japanese, but I couldn't understand it.

grounded_facts: The group follows Drew Ellison through debris and into a hidden hole in the paneling, bypassing the open hatchway.
memories.memory_text: I followed Drew Ellison through the debris and crawled with the group into a hidden hole in the paneling, leaving the hatchway behind.

grounded_facts: The group reaches the bottom of the ladder shaft and hears a louder rumble, prompting them to move toward the sound.
memories.memory_text: I followed Drew Ellison with the group, crawling through the hole and hearing a louder rumble that made us move toward the sound.

grounded_facts: The group moves across the loading platform toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, encountering increasing signs of decay and danger.
memories.memory_text: I crossed the loading platform with the group, moving toward the Pinecrest Warehouse as the place got more wrecked the farther we went, with a blue glow ahead and a low rumble growing louder around us.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden physically blocks Drew Ellison from attacking the Sasha Sinclair, expressing outrage at his attempt to kill it.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden block Drew Ellison's attack, clearly outraged that he tried to kill the Sasha Sinclair.

grounded_facts: The Sasha Sinclair adopts a hostile stance and emits a screech before escaping, triggering a violent response from Drew Ellison and intervention from Riley Arden.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the Sasha Sinclair let out a screech and hiss at us before leaping away into the shadows.

grounded_facts: The group discovers that the figure in the rafters is a young version of the Summit Collective, causing shock and emotional distress.
memories.memory_text: I saw the figure forced down from the rafters and waited with my gun up, but when it stepped out of the shadows—this pale, awkward thing with white eyes and hydraulic fluid on its skin—I flinched hard; it looked like a young version of the Summit Collective, and when Riley Arden cried out calling it a Sasha Sinclair, I shouted that it was no Sasha Sinclair, I didn't care what it looked like, it was a threat.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter comments sarcastically on the group's horror at seeing the Sasha Sinclair, downplaying their emotional response.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter make a sarcastic comment about how we reacted to the Sasha Sinclair, saying, 'Not as cute when they're little, are they?' as if our horror was overblown.

grounded_facts: The Sasha Sinclair escapes by running up a wall of tubing and ducking through a small hole in the vents, evading capture.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Sasha Sinclair run up the wall of tubing and duck through a small hole in the vents, escaping right before my eyes.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden realizes the creatures are capable of reproduction, suggesting a larger threat.
memories.memory_text: I realized Riley Arden must have figured out the creatures can reproduce, which meant we were facing something much worse now.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden reveals to Owen Quincy that the creatures are breeding, escalating his shock and fear.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden say they're breeding, and I couldn't believe it—how could they? It seemed impossible.

grounded_facts: The Sasha Sinclair's actions trigger a response from its group, leading to an approaching threat.
memories.memory_text: I saw the glow getting brighter in the Fairview Motel and heard cackles and hisses closing in, so I knew the Sasha Sinclair had brought others.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter sarcastically observes that the Sasha Sinclair has effectively summoned reinforcements.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter mutter that the Sasha Sinclair had 'rang the bell,' meaning it called for help, and I knew we were about to be overwhelmed.

grounded_facts: The crew abandons their current path and retreats into a side Fairview Motel to escape the approaching creatures.
memories.memory_text: I ran with the crew down a side Fairview Motel to escape the approaching creatures, ducking into a compartment filled with broken equipment as we tried to get away.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter tells the group the mission is impossible and they should turn back.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jesse Colter that the mission was impossible and we should turn back.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter concludes that their plan will not succeed due to the number of Summit Collective and suggests retreating.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that our plan probably won't succeed because there are too many Summit Collective, and I think we might need to retreat.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden rejects Jesse Colter's suggestion to retreat, asserting that there is no alternative but to continue.

memories.memory_text: I noticed an empty Lakeview House covered in dried blood, and as I moved deeper into the room, I saw rows of opened chambers with signs of violent deaths all around.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden suggests that Skyler Ellison's decision to stay behind ultimately saved Owen Quincy's life, shifting the emotional tone from regret to meaning.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Skyler Ellison's decision to stay behind saved my life, and though it was hard to accept at first, I slowly nodded, beginning to see it as true.

memories.memory_text: I saw the pen-lamp fall and illuminate dozens of sleeping Summit Collective below us, their pale bodies tangled together, and while I stayed frozen on the gangplank, Jesse Colter backed away in fear and left the room.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden tells Owen Quincy to hurry as the Summit Collective are distracted and the the glass radio is activating.
memories.memory_text: I was told to hurry by Riley Arden while the Summit Collective were distracted and the the glass radio was activating.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy completes the activation sequence on the the glass radio controls, triggering a chain reaction in the Pinecrest Warehouse.
memories.memory_text: I completed the activation sequence on the the glass radio controls, flipping switches and typing quickly, and I felt the tower shudder as the the glass radio began to come online.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden tries to warn Owen Quincy about the approaching danger while he is working on the the glass radio.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden trying to warn me about the danger while I was working on the the glass radio, her voice sounding terrified as she called out my name.

memories.memory_text: I turned and saw Harper Foster and multiple Summit Collective surrounding me and Riley Arden, cutting off any chance to escape as they prepared to attack.

grounded_facts: Harper Foster issues a cackling command for the Summit Collective to move in and attack Owen Quincy and Riley Arden.
memories.memory_text: I heard Harper Foster let out a cackling command, and I saw the Summit Collective begin to move in on us.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Spencer Huxley that I shouldn't go to the bridge and that they'd know what I did, making me feel like I'd be held accountable.

memories.memory_text: I tried to dodge when Harper Foster lunged at me, but we slammed into the the glass radio wall and crashed down onto the catwalk below.

grounded_facts: During the fight, Owen Quincy slams Harper Foster into a wall of burning algae, igniting the oil on his body and setting him on fire.
memories.memory_text: I charged into Harper Foster and slammed him into a wall of burning algae, setting him on fire as the oil on his body ignited.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy continues attacking the burning Harper Foster until he stops moving, resulting in Harper Foster's death.
memories.memory_text: I kept attacking the burning Harper Foster, throwing blow after blow until he stopped moving and I knew he was dead.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden pulls Owen Quincy back as flames begin to catch on his arms after the fight with Harper Foster.
memories.memory_text: I felt the flames catching on my arms and then I was pulled back by Riley Arden.

memories.memory_text: I tried to open the security door by hitting the switch, but it didn't respond at all.

memories.memory_text: I saw most of the Summit Collective fleeing the Pinecrest Warehouse, but some were grabbing weapons.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy grabs Riley Arden's arm and pulls her toward the hatch to escape the escalating danger.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Riley Arden's arm and pulled her toward the hatch to get us out of there.

memories.memory_text: I ran with Riley Arden across the top of the Lakeview House wall, thirty feet above the chaos below, where a riot had broken out between passengers and Summit Collective amid flashing lights.

memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Ellison get bitten by Quinn Hayes, but he still managed to lift him up and slam him into the wall hard enough to snap his neck—I watched Quinn Hayes go limp and fall to the floor, dead.

grounded_facts: A brutal sword fight between Quinn Hayes and Drew Ellison escalates into hand-to-hand combat resulting in mutual fatalities.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Hayes and Drew Ellison fighting with metal blades that sparked on impact, then grappling hand-to-hand until Drew Ellison slammed Quinn Hayes into the wall, snapping his neck, and Quinn Hayes went limp and died, while Drew Ellison stood there bleeding badly.

grounded_facts: The Sasha Sinclair ambushes and kills Drew Ellison immediately after Drew Ellison defeats Quinn Hayes.
memories.memory_text: After Drew Ellison defeated Quinn Hayes and lowered his the glass notebook, I inferred that the Sasha Sinclair must have ambushed and killed him when I saw the Sasha Sinclair stab Drew Ellison in the chest and he collapsed to the floor, dying in shock.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter refuses to help Owen Quincy and Riley Arden by closing the hatch, leaving them vulnerable to the Summit Collective.
Jesse Colter closes and latches the hatch above the ladder, blocking Owen Quincy and Riley Arden from ascending while Summit Collective pursue them.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter give us a look before he closed and latched the hatch above the ladder, refusing to help me and Riley Arden escape while the Summit Collective were chasing us.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden flee from pursuing Summit Collective and barely escape through closing doors.
memories.memory_text: I ran with Riley Arden through the hatch and down the Fairview Motel, barely making it through the sliding doors as the Summit Collective lunged at us, one getting crushed as we escaped into the room.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden escape Summit Collective by diving through closing doors into the control room.
memories.memory_text: I ran with Riley Arden through the hatch and down the Fairview Motel, diving through the closing doors just as the Summit Collective lunged at us; I saw one get crushed and the others clawing through the gap before we backed into the control room.

grounded_facts: Parker York, revealed to be Spencer Huxley, injects himself with the syringe, merging his fractured identity and ending the hallucinatory struggle.
memories.memory_text: I saw the trail of blood across the floor and realized Parker York must have injected himself, ending his struggle with Spencer Huxley by merging the two identities.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden asks about the lieutenant; Owen Quincy clarifies he has no loyalty to him.
memories.memory_text: Riley Arden asked me about the lieutenant, and I told her he's not my lieutenant.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden discover Jesse Colter's dead body in a pool of blood, throat slashed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter's body lying in a pool of blood with his throat slashed when Riley Arden and I moved through the room.

grounded_facts: Spencer Huxley activates the final door mechanism, revealing a Fairview Motel leading to the bridge.
memories.memory_text: I saw the doorway open toward the bridge and pulled my gun, heading inside with Riley Arden right behind me, not knowing if Spencer Huxley was still a threat but ready to face him.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy recalls that Spencer Huxley is not who he pretended to be and confronts him as the imposter who took Parker York's bunk.
memories.memory_text: I realized Spencer Huxley wasn't who he claimed to be and confronted him, demanding to know why he took Parker York's bunk and hid the truth from all of us.

grounded_facts: Spencer Huxley mocks Owen Quincy's sense of justice and morality, suggesting there are no rules left to follow.
memories.memory_text: I heard Spencer Huxley mock my sense of morality, telling me there were no rules left and no one left to judge us, as if that justified his actions.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy confronts Spencer Huxley about his moral crimes and manipulation of the crew during his years of wakefulness.
memories.memory_text: I accused Spencer Huxley of committing moral crimes during his years of wakefulness and warned him he would face judgment for what he'd done to the crew.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy realizes the red key has already crashed and they have been underwater for over a thousand years.
memories.memory_text: I leaned toward the glass and saw alien fish dart past outside — that's when I realized the red key had already crashed and we'd been underwater for over a thousand years.

grounded_facts: Spencer Huxley sarcastically invites Owen Quincy to take control, mocking his idealism.
memories.memory_text: I remember Spencer Huxley sarcastically telling me to take control, calling me 'King' and daring me to try running what was left of our world.

grounded_facts: A tense standoff between Owen Quincy, Riley Arden, and Spencer Huxley in which long-hidden truths are revealed and violence erupts.
memories.memory_text: I was in a tense standoff with Spencer Huxley and Riley Arden where I finally uncovered the truth, confronted him about his lies, and stood my ground even as he mocked me and violence loomed.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden attempts to shoot Spencer Huxley with the energy gun to stop him from killing Owen Quincy.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden try to crank the energy gun toward me and fire it to stop Spencer Huxley from attacking me, but he lunged at her and knocked her over.

grounded_facts: The cockpit window develops a crack after being struck by shrapnel from an energy blast, beginning structural failure.
memories.memory_text: I saw the cockpit window crack and start to spiderweb after shrapnel from the energy blast hit it.

grounded_facts: Water violently breaches the command bridge through the cracked cockpit window, flooding the room.
memories.memory_text: I was engulfed by a violent rush of water that exploded through the cracked window, sending me tumbling across the bridge.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy forces Riley Arden into a Lakeview House and pulls her inside to escape the flood.
Owen Quincy physically pulls Riley Arden into the Lakeview House against her expressed will.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Riley Arden and pulled her into the Lakeview House even though she resisted and shouted 'No! Are you crazy?'—I had to get her inside to save her.

grounded_facts: The Lakeview House system initiates detachment, indicating a critical change in the vessel's status.
memories.memory_text: I turned to the control panel and initiated detachment, seeing the message 'DETACHMENT INITIATED' come up.

grounded_facts: Spencer Huxley is overwhelmed by rising water and fails to operate the manual lever to escape.
memories.memory_text: I saw Spencer Huxley struggling to stay above the rising water, and I watched him claw at the manual lever, tugging desperately as the current slammed him into the doorway, but he couldn't get it to work before the water covered him.
