grounded_facts: The pod violently collides with an object, causing sparks, seal ruptures, and water intrusion under high pressure.
memories.memory_text: I felt the pod slam into something hard, sparks flying as the seals ruptured and water blasted in, throwing me and Riley Arden around like we were in a washing machine.

grounded_facts: Water washes over the control panel, causing a final burst of sparks that knocks out all lights and power.
memories.memory_text: I saw the water wash over the control panel and spark violently before all the lights went out and we were plunged into darkness.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy insists and physically places the oxygen mask on Riley Arden despite her resistance, prioritizing her survival over his own.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Owen Quincy insists and physically places the oxygen mask on Riley Arden despite her resistance, prioritizing her survival over his own.

grounded_facts: A high-stakes emergency sequence involving the launch, collision, and flooding of an escape pod carrying Owen Quincy and Riley Arden.
memories.memory_text: I was crammed in the pod with Riley Arden as water rose fast, then we were slammed by impacts, sparks flew, and water blasted in—I forced the oxygen mask onto her, gasped my last breath as the water covered my head, and watched her go limp while a bright light grew outside.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy forces the oxygen mask onto Riley Arden as the last air pocket shrinks, allowing her to breathe while he is left without.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Owen Quincy forces the oxygen mask onto Riley Arden as the last air pocket shrinks, allowing her to breathe while he is left without.

grounded_facts: A growing glow of white light enters through the porthole, revealing sunlight, indicating the pod has surfaced or entered a lit environment.
memories.memory_text: I saw a growing glow of white light through the porthole, and realized it was sunlight, so I started kicking at the hatch to get out.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden regains consciousness after being pulled from the chamber and having her mask removed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden's eyes begin to flicker as she regained consciousness after I pulled her out and removed her mask.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy comforts Riley Arden as she wakes, telling her it's safe to wake up this time.
memories.memory_text: I pulled Riley Arden out of the chamber and ripped the mask off her face, then told her it was safe to wake up this time.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden realize they are on an alien world with multiple moons and unfamiliar geography.
memories.memory_text: I turned with Riley Arden to see our surroundings and realized we were on an alien world, with strange islands and multiple moons in the sky.

grounded_facts: A moment of emergence and reorientation as Owen Quincy and Riley Arden surface from a submerged chamber into a strange new world.
Owen Quincy and Riley Arden emerge from the Lakeview House to the ocean surface, escaping their previous submerged state.
memories.memory_text: I kicked open the hatch and gasped for air, then pulled Riley Arden out of the chamber and ripped the mask off her face; we were floating on the ocean surface, and when I looked around, I saw strange islands and multiple moons in the sky—this wasn't Earth.

grounded_facts: A violent encounter and subsequent de-escalation involving Owen Quincy, Drew Ellison, and Riley Arden in a recreational room.
memories.memory_text: I was in the rec room when Owen Quincy got attacked, and I jumped in to help him, using a pipe to strike the attacker. Then Riley Arden threw a pool ball at me, and everything escalated until Owen Quincy fired a warning shot that knocked us all back. I remember trying to find my the glass notebook after that, and eventually backing toward the door with Owen Quincy after he called us off.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison gestures to her uniform emblem and grins, indicating mutual understanding and willingness to cooperate.
memories.memory_text: I gestured to the emblem on my uniform and grinned, showing that I understood and was willing to cooperate.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy advocates for collaboration among the three characters to increase chances of survival and escape.
Owen Quincy suggests that they work together for mutual survival and escape.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Owen Quincy that we should work together for mutual survival and escape, and he said we all want the same thing as long as we understand each other.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy demands to know who Riley Arden is after she interrupts them, seeking to establish her role and threat level.
memories.memory_text: I heard Owen Quincy demand to know who Riley Arden was, asking her to give her name like it was some kind of team requirement.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden informs Owen Quincy and Drew Ellison that they are heading in the wrong direction toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, providing critical navigational information.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden tell Owen Quincy that we were going the wrong way toward the Pinecrest Warehouse and that she didn’t want to go there because no one ever came back, so I realized our direction was a mistake.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy physically grabs Riley Arden's arm to stop her from leaving, leading to a moment of tension and resistance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy grab Riley Arden's arm when she tried to leave, and I watched her yank away, standing her ground with her the glass notebook ready.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden tests Owen Quincy's competence by asking if he can actually fly the red key, assessing his usefulness and credibility.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden questioning Owen Quincy, asking if he could actually fly the red key and whether he could do it if he had to, like she was testing him.

grounded_facts: After being questioned and challenged, Riley Arden agrees to lead Owen Quincy toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, though she refuses to wait for him.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Riley Arden agree to lead Owen Quincy toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, though she made it clear she wouldn't wait for him, and then she just walked off.

grounded_facts: An unplanned meeting in the Fairview Motel between Owen Quincy, Drew Ellison, and Riley Arden that results in critical information exchange and a temporary coordination of movement.
memories.memory_text: I was with Owen Quincy in the Fairview Motel, trying to get through a sealed door, when Riley Arden suddenly appeared and confronted us; we were both on edge, but she stayed calm and questioned who we were and where we were going before telling us we were headed in the wrong direction and then moving off down the hall after Owen Quincy asked her to lead the way.

grounded_facts: Bolter asks Riley Arden if she knows where she is going and expresses discomfort with the environment.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bolter ask Riley Arden if she knew where she was going and say that the environment didn't feel right.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden sharply tells Owen Quincy to be quiet, warning that his loud voice could get them killed.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden sharply tell Owen Quincy to be quiet, warning that his loud voice could get us killed.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy expresses shock and disbelief upon hearing that people have been awake for months.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy react with shock when he heard people had been awake for months, yelling 'MONTHS!?' and demanding to know how that could be.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden discloses that she has been awake for two to three months, indicating she was not the first to awaken.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden saying she had been awake for two to three months and that she wasn't the first to wake up.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden leads Owen Quincy and Drew Ellison through a large atrium with multiple shafts, moving toward a side shaft.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden leading Owen Quincy and me through a large atrium filled with shafts and then down into a side shaft.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden silences Owen Quincy twice to prevent noise that might alert the Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden silence Owen Quincy twice with sharp warnings—first saying 'Shush! We're waiting,' and then just 'Quiet!'—to keep him from making noise that might alert the Summit Collective closing in on us.

grounded_facts: The group observes a bluish glow and moving shadows indicating the approach of Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I saw a bluish glow at the end of the Fairview Motel and noticed shadows moving closer, which made me realize something was coming.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy physically stops Drew Ellison from fleeing as the Summit Collective approach.
memories.memory_text: I wanted to run when I saw the Summit Collective approaching, but Owen Quincy grabbed my shoulder and stopped me from fleeing.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden attempts to open the vault door using a hand scanner, but the power surge cuts out, leaving the door only partially open.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden try to open the vault door using the hand scanner during the power surge, but the power cut out too soon and the door only opened a half foot; we had to squeeze through and then help her push it shut to seal it.

grounded_facts: The group arrives at the steel vault door and takes cover, initiating a waiting phase under Riley Arden's direction.
A tense confrontation at the bio-lab vault door as the group evades approaching Summit Collective and attempts to gain entry.
memories.memory_text: I remember arriving at the steel vault door with the group and taking cover in the shadows under Riley Arden's direction, waiting as the bluish glow and moving shadows grew closer down the Fairview Motel, knowing the Summit Collective were approaching and we had to stay quiet to avoid them.

grounded_facts: The group squeezes through the partially open vault door and manually pushes it shut, sealing themselves inside.
memories.memory_text: I squeezed through the half-foot gap in the vault door and helped Owen Quincy and the others push it shut, hearing a loud clank as we sealed it behind us.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy realizes that the Lakeview House in the Lakeview House hyper-sleep compartment are all empty, leading to concern about the missing crew.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy react with shock when he realized all the Lakeview House were empty, and I heard him say, 'My God. They're... empty. They're all— Where the hell is everyone?'

grounded_facts: Riley Arden dismisses Owen Quincy's attempt to search for his Jesse Nolan by informing him that family members are not housed in this section.
memories.memory_text: I remember when Owen Quincy stopped to look for his Jesse Nolan, and Riley Arden told him she wouldn't be in this section because it was only for engineers and development settlers.

grounded_facts: The group enters the Lakeview House to investigate the status of the crew and navigate through the damaged facility.
memories.memory_text: I was with the group when we entered the Lakeview House to check on the crew, moving carefully through the damaged facility.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden repeatedly orders Owen Quincy to stay quiet and keep moving, asserting control over the situation due to perceived danger.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden repeatedly telling Owen Quincy to keep quiet and keep moving, insisting we couldn't stay in the open because of the danger.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy calls out to Drew Ellison to rejoin the group as they prepare to leave the area.
memories.memory_text: I heard Owen Quincy call out to me, telling me to come on and leave with them.

grounded_facts: The group abandons Drew Ellison as he remains fixated on a distant threat, while Owen Quincy follows Riley Arden away, leaving Drew Ellison behind.
memories.memory_text: I stayed focused on the threat in the dark while the others left, and I moved into the shadows alone.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy stops moving and focuses on checking the nameplates of the Lakeview House, hoping to find his Jesse Nolan among the settlers.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy hesitate and then start checking the nameplates on the Lakeview House, clearly hoping to find his Jesse Nolan among the people there.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden grabs Owen Quincy to stop him from speaking when a Nico Adler is nearby.
memories.memory_text: I saw Riley Arden suddenly grab Owen Quincy to silence him just as a shadow passed with a cackling hiss, and we all froze where we lay on the bones beneath us.

grounded_facts: Faced with the choice of waiting for Drew Ellison or following Riley Arden, Owen Quincy chooses to chase after her.
memories.memory_text: I think Owen Quincy hesitated, trying to decide whether to wait for me or follow Riley Arden, and in the end he must have chosen to chase after her.

grounded_facts: A Nico Adler appears and attacks Owen Quincy and Riley Arden, leading to a violent confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Nico Adler appear and attack Owen Quincy and Riley Arden, so I lunged out of the shadows with my bladed pipe and joined them in fighting it, knowing we had to bring it down together before more arrived.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison emerges from the shadows and attacks the Nico Adler, turning the tide of the battle.
memories.memory_text: I lunged out of the shadows and struck the Nico Adler with my bladed pipe, but it hit me back hard—nearly knocked me out. I saw Owen Quincy and Riley Arden react, and then I realized more Summit Collective were coming, drawn by the noise.

grounded_facts: Quinn Hayes taps his spear, signaling other Summit Collective and causing the room to fill with them.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Hayes tap his spear, and right away the room began filling with Summit Collective as shadows moved around us.

grounded_facts: After defeating one Nico Adler and seeing more arrive, the group decides to run.
memories.memory_text: I helped Owen Quincy and Riley Arden take down one Nico Adler, but then I saw shadows moving and realized more were coming; I heard Riley Arden shout 'Run!' and I followed her and Owen Quincy as we fled the chamber with Summit Collective swarming in.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy argues that Drew Ellison saved his life and should not be abandoned.
memories.memory_text: I remember Owen Quincy shouting that I saved his life and that they shouldn't leave me behind as we ran through the chamber, the Summit Collective swarming around us.

grounded_facts: A tense and horrifying confrontation in a chamber filled with human remains, where the group faces a Nico Adler and is subsequently ambushed by more.
memories.memory_text: I lunged at the Nico Adler from the shadows and struck it, but it hit me hard and nearly knocked me out; we all fought it together under flickering light, and after we brought it down, I saw the room filling with more Summit Collective moving in the dark.

grounded_facts: After the group escapes, Quinn Hayes and his pack pause to eat the defeated Nico Adler.
memories.memory_text: I was fleeing with the group when I realized Quinn Hayes and his pack had stopped to eat the fallen Nico Adler—I didn’t see it directly, but it made sense in the moment why they’d paused.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden crawl out of the hatch door into the main Fairview Motel, joining Drew Ellison who is already waiting.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy and Riley Arden crawl out of the hatch and join me in the main Fairview Motel.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy urges immediate action to flee, while Riley Arden suggests returning to find another path, leading to tension.
memories.memory_text: I heard Owen Quincy urge us to flee right away, while Riley Arden argued for going back to find another path, and their argument created tension between them.

grounded_facts: A power surge causes flickering lights and activates a blinking light on a sleep-chamber; shortly after, the hatch is violently kicked open with white gas escaping.
memories.memory_text: I saw the lights flicker from a power surge, and then the hatch was kicked open with white gas bursting out, so I quickly crawled to the shadows with the others to hide.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy attempts to stand and help the Big Passenger, but Riley Arden pulls him back to prevent detection.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy try to stand up to help the Big Passenger, and I heard Riley Arden yell at him while pulling him back.

grounded_facts: As Owen Quincy attempts to intervene during the Summit Collective' attack, Drew Ellison forcibly grabs and holds him back.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Owen Quincy and held him back when he tried to break away and intervene during the attack.

grounded_facts: A Big Passenger crawls out of the hatch, struggling physically, then is struck by Quinn Hayes and captured by the Summit Collective.
memories.memory_text: I watched the Big Passenger crawl out, struggling and gasping, then get struck by Quinn Hayes and surrounded by the Summit Collective who captured and began attacking it while praying.

grounded_facts: The Summit Collective gather in a circle around the wounded Big Passenger, perform a ceremonial prayer, and then consume him in a frenzied, ritualistic manner.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the Summit Collective surround the wounded Big Passenger, perform a ceremonial prayer, and then tear him apart in a frenzied ritual while Harper Foster led a twisted dance under the flickering lights.

grounded_facts: The Summit Collective gather around the wounded Big Passenger, perform a ceremonial ritual, and then brutally attack and eat him alive.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Summit Collective return and knock down the Big Passenger, then gather in a circle around him, giving thanks before they attacked and started eating him alive while Harper Foster led a wild dance in the flickering light.

grounded_facts: After witnessing the attack, Owen Quincy, Riley Arden, and Drew Ellison retreat to a corner where Riley Arden lifts a floor grate; they climb into a dark shaft to escape.
memories.memory_text: After seeing what happened, I helped pull Owen Quincy with us as we fled to the corner, climbed through the floor grate, and escaped into the dark shaft.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy challenges Riley Arden's leadership and decision-making during their escape attempt.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy directly challenge Riley Arden's leadership, demanding to know if she even knew where she was going and complaining that we were just running in circles down here.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden justifies her involvement by emphasizing her role in saving Owen Quincy.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden justify her actions by shouting that she didn't have to help Owen Quincy at all—that he'd still be trapped on level eight without her intervention.

grounded_facts: Tension rises between Owen Quincy and Riley Arden over the purpose and direction of their journey, revealing distrust.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the tension rise between Owen Quincy and Riley Arden as they argued about the direction of our escape—Owen Quincy质疑 her leadership, and Riley Arden fired back, defending her choices and reminding him she saved his life.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison halts the argument between Owen Quincy and Riley Arden by drawing attention to an external sound.
memories.memory_text: I halted Owen Quincy and Riley Arden's argument by hissing for silence and drawing their attention to a sound—I heard classical music echoing from below, and we all stopped to listen.

grounded_facts: The group discovers a concealed, habitable area inside a storage tank, suggesting prior human activity and survival efforts.
memories.memory_text: I heard classical music echoing from below and followed the sound with the group, peering into an open hatch before I began climbing through—it was clear someone had been living inside that storage tank.

grounded_facts: A group effort to navigate and escape from a confined, industrial sub-level environment.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the group effort to escape the industrial sub-level, trying to pry open grates and eventually climbing through when we found a way out, though Riley Arden hesitated at the last moment.

grounded_facts: The hatch to the tank closes suddenly due to a triggered trap, trapping Drew Ellison, Riley Arden, and Owen Quincy inside.
memories.memory_text: I was right there when the hatch slammed shut the moment Riley Arden stepped through — a wire snapped and the trap triggered, trapping me, Riley Arden, and Owen Quincy inside.

grounded_facts: A stream of colorless chemical gas is released into the tank, causing the characters to choke.
memories.memory_text: I choked as a stream of colorless gas shot into the tank and hit me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter shouts at Drew Ellison to stop climbing and return, attempting to prevent his ascent.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter shout at me to stop climbing and get back down.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison attempts to climb the slanted wall and reach the catwalk but is forced to let go after being jabbed by Jesse Colter with a spear.
memories.memory_text: I tried to climb the wall to reach the catwalk, but Jesse Colter jabbed my hand with a spear and I lost my grip, falling back down.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy fires an the glass notebook at the hatch, creating a spark that ignites the chemical gas.
The chemical gas is ignited by the energy blast, causing a burst of flame that rolls into the catwalks and knocks Jesse Colter off his feet.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy fire his the glass notebook at the hatch, and the spark from the blast ignited the chemical gas, causing a burst of flame that rolled into the catwalks and knocked Jesse Colter off his feet.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy points his the glass notebook at Jesse Colter and demands he shut off the gas.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy whirl the lever on his the glass notebook and point it at Jesse Colter, and I inferred he was threatening him to shut off the gas.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter expresses surprise and asks Owen Quincy where he got the the glass notebook.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Colter asking me, 'Where did you get that?' after seeing the the glass notebook in action, like he couldn't believe I had something so powerful.

grounded_facts: Under threat from Owen Quincy, Jesse Colter shuts off the flow of chemical gas by manipulating levers and nozzles.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Jesse Colter scurrying across the catwalk and lifting levers to shut off the flow of chemical gas.

grounded_facts: After shutting off the gas, Jesse Colter reacts with curiosity and offers to trade for the the glass notebook.
Jesse Colter, after seeing the the glass notebook's power, suggests trading for it.
memories.memory_text: After I shut off the gas, I saw Jesse Colter go from scared to curious—he stared into the barrel of my the glass notebook and then asked if I was looking to trade, like he wanted it for himself.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter cranks an energy lever to turn on auxiliary lights, expanding visibility in the water processor room.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter crank an energy lever that turned on a string of auxiliary lights, suddenly illuminating the whole water processor room.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy asks Jesse Colter to come down to meet properly, but Jesse Colter refuses due to fear of contamination.
memories.memory_text: I heard Owen Quincy ask Jesse Colter to come down and meet us properly, but Jesse Colter refused, saying he was too worried about catching something from us because of the dust bug.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter lowers a bin of food via wire for the group, claiming it is kosher.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter lower a bin of food down to us with a wire, and I sniffed it suspiciously because I wasn't sure if it was safe, but he claimed it was kosher.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter greets and interacts with Owen Quincy, Riley Arden, and Drew Ellison in the water processor, offering food and information.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Colter welcomed me along with Owen Quincy and Riley Arden, telling us to make ourselves at home and not to pet the rat, and later said the food was Kosher when offering it.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy asks Jesse Colter about the Pinecrest Warehouse, confirming Jesse Colter has knowledge of the red key layout.
memories.memory_text: I heard Owen Quincy ask Jesse Colter if he knew where the Pinecrest Warehouse was, and Jesse Colter responded with a grin, hinting that he knew more than he let on.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter cooks a makeshift soup using powder and heated water, treating the act with exaggerated care and humor.
memories.memory_text: I watched Jesse Colter carefully stir that powder into hot water like it was some gourmet dish, making a big show of it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter admits he has lost track of time, referencing having stopped counting after a band broke up decades ago, and comments on time distortion in the red key.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter say he stopped counting time after a band broke up decades ago, and it made me realize how distorted everything feels on this the red key.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter makes a sarcastic comment about writing a complaint to the airline, reflecting disillusionment and coping through irony.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Colter saying he was going to write a strongly worded letter to the airline, deadpan like he actually meant it, as some kind of joke.

grounded_facts: An informal gathering where Jesse Colter distributes soup to the group, attempting to create a moment of normalcy and connection.
Jesse Colter lowers bowls of soup to the others, framing it as a festive ritual.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Colter lower bowls of soup down to us like it was some kind of ceremony, trying to make it feel normal, like we were just sharing a meal together.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy speculates whether the creatures came from Jesse Colter's lab or boarded the red key, prompting Riley Arden's theory.
memories.memory_text: I heard Owen Quincy ask if the creatures could have come from Jesse Colter's lab or if something had boarded the red key.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden suggests that the creatures may have originated from the synthetic enzyme 'accelerator' in the feeding tubes, which was meant to help humans adapt to Tanis but instead caused the creatures to adapt to the red key environment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden saying the creatures might have come from the synthetic enzyme 'accelerator' in the feeding tubes, meant to help us adapt to Tanis but instead causing them to adapt to the red key.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison shakes his head and gestures to stop Owen Quincy from entering the hatchway, conveying caution non-verbally.
memories.memory_text: I shook my head and gestured to stop Owen Quincy from entering the hatchway, silently warning him of danger.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison physically stops Owen Quincy from entering through the hatchway, indicating danger or caution.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Owen Quincy and pulled him back to physically stop him from going through the hatchway because I knew it was unsafe.

grounded_facts: The group follows Drew Ellison through debris and into a hidden hole in the paneling, bypassing the open hatchway.
memories.memory_text: I led the group through the debris and into a hidden hole in the paneling, and they followed me as I guided them along the concealed path.

grounded_facts: The group reaches the bottom of the ladder shaft and hears a louder rumble, prompting them to move toward the sound.
memories.memory_text: I heard a louder rumble when we reached the bottom of the ladder shaft, and I knew we had to move toward the sound.

grounded_facts: The group moves across the loading platform toward the Pinecrest Warehouse, encountering increasing signs of decay and danger.
memories.memory_text: I remember crossing the loading platform with the group, seeing how the place had fallen apart over time—battle scars everywhere, the walls battered, and that blue glow ahead pulsing stronger as we moved forward, the rumble beneath our feet growing louder.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden physically blocks Drew Ellison from attacking the Sasha Sinclair, expressing outrage at his attempt to kill it.
memories.memory_text: I lunged at the Sasha Sinclair, but Riley Arden blocked me, stopping my attack and showing her outrage at what I tried to do.

grounded_facts: The Sasha Sinclair adopts a hostile stance and emits a screech before escaping, triggering a violent response from Drew Ellison and intervention from Riley Arden.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Sasha Sinclair let out a horrific screech and hiss at us before leaping away and vanishing into the shadows above.

grounded_facts: The group discovers that the figure in the rafters is a young version of the Summit Collective, causing shock and emotional distress.
memories.memory_text: I saw it step out of the shadows—a Sasha Sinclair, a young version of the Summit Collective, pale and slick with fluid, its oblong head and white eyes hidden under a membrane, then it let out a screech and hissed at us before leaping back into the rafters and vanishing, and I felt my breath catch in shock.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter comments sarcastically on the group's horror at seeing the Sasha Sinclair, downplaying their emotional response.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter make a sarcastic comment about how we reacted to the Sasha Sinclair, saying, 'Not as cute when they're little, are they?' as if our horror wasn't justified.

grounded_facts: The Sasha Sinclair escapes by running up a wall of tubing and ducking through a small hole in the vents, evading capture.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Sasha Sinclair run up the wall of tubing and duck through a small hole in the vents, escaping right before our eyes.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden realizes the creatures are capable of reproduction, suggesting a larger threat.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden say, 'My God. They're... breeding,' and realized in that moment the creatures could reproduce, which made the danger feel much larger.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden reveals to Owen Quincy that the creatures are breeding, escalating his shock and fear.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riley Arden that the creatures are breeding, and I saw Owen Quincy react with shock, yelling that it was impossible.

grounded_facts: The Sasha Sinclair's actions trigger a response from its group, leading to an approaching threat.
memories.memory_text: I saw the bluish glow growing stronger in the Fairview Motel and heard cackles and hisses approaching, realizing the Sasha Sinclair had alerted its group and they were coming toward us.

grounded_facts: Jesse Colter sarcastically observes that the Sasha Sinclair has effectively summoned reinforcements.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Colter say sarcastically, 'Little bastard rang the bell,' meaning the Sasha Sinclair had summoned reinforcements.

grounded_facts: The crew abandons their current path and retreats into a side Fairview Motel to escape the approaching creatures.
memories.memory_text: I ran with the crew down a side Fairview Motel to escape the approaching creatures, fleeing into a compartment filled with broken equipment.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden presses Owen Quincy on his actions and emotional state upon seeing the chambers, leading him to reveal his grief over Skyler Ellison.
memories.memory_text: I remember Riley Arden asking me what was wrong and if I thought Skyler Ellison was there, pressing me about my reaction as we stood among the chambers.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy concludes that Skyler Ellison is not on the red key and is dead, explaining she chose not to join him, which motivated his departure from Earth.
memories.memory_text: I told Riley Arden that Skyler Ellison isn't on the red key and that she's dead, explaining she chose not to come with me or marry me, and that's why I left Earth—there was nothing left for me after she stayed behind.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy and Riley Arden enter and move through a compartment filled with opened and bloodied Lakeview House, investigating signs of violence and personal connections.
memories.memory_text: I moved through the compartment with Riley Arden, seeing the opened Lakeview House and blood everywhere, and I could feel my jaw tighten as I gripped my the glass notebook and prepared to keep going.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy ignores Jesse Colter's fearful pleas and continues descending into the Pinecrest Warehouse.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy ignore Jesse Colter's fearful pleas and just keep descending into the Pinecrest Warehouse, so I followed right after.

grounded_facts: Riley Arden orders Jesse Colter to be quiet and move forward during the descent.
memories.memory_text: I heard Riley Arden shout at Jesse Colter to shut up and move forward during the descent.

grounded_facts: The team enters the Pinecrest Warehouse and begins a dangerous descent down the catwalks toward the the glass radio core.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the team that entered the Pinecrest Warehouse and began the dangerous descent down the catwalks toward the core, clinging to pipes and railings as the glowing algae grew denser below us.

grounded_facts: While crossing the gangplank, Owen Quincy grabs a vine that breaks, causing him to dangle over the edge before being rescued by Riley Arden.
Riley Arden jumps across a gap and extends her the glass notebook for Owen Quincy to grab after he loses his grip on a vine.
memories.memory_text: I watched in fright as Owen Quincy lost his grip on a vine and dangled over the edge, and then I saw Riley Arden jump across the gap and extend her the glass notebook for him to grab so he could be pulled to safety.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy attempts to activate the control panel but initially fails, then begins pumping a primer switch as the panel flickers.
memories.memory_text: I watched Owen Quincy crawl to the control panel and try to activate it, but nothing happened at first, and then I saw him start pumping a primer switch as the panel began to flicker.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison draws the Summit Collective' attention by striking the railing and throwing his the glass notebook, then escapes through a hatch to divert them.
memories.memory_text: I banged my the glass notebook against the railing to get the Summit Collective' attention, then threw it at one of them and broke through a hatch to lead them away.

grounded_facts: Owen Quincy successfully activates the Pinecrest Warehouse, bringing the panels to life and initiating the rotation sequence.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Quincy crank the hand lever and hit the primer switch, then flip more switches as the the glass radio began to hum and the panels came to life.

grounded_facts: Quinn Hayes and the remaining Summit Collective try to cut through the tangled snare created by the booby-trap to continue the pursuit.
memories.memory_text: I could hear the Summit Collective behind me, crashing through the debris as I ran—I knew they were trying to cut through the snare I'd triggered, desperate to keep chasing me.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison dives through the open hatchway just as a pursuing Nico Adler is about to catch him, narrowly escaping.
memories.memory_text: I dove through the open hatchway just as the Nico Adler was almost upon me, feeling the rush of danger as I barely escaped.

grounded_facts: A booby-trap activates as a Nico Adler follows Drew Ellison, resulting in the Nico Adler being nearly cut in half by a razor-wire clothesline.
memories.memory_text: I heard the snap of hydraulic pistons and knew the booby-trap had fired; I didn't look back but felt the razor-wire clothesline the Nico Adler following me, nearly cutting him in half as I hit the floor and kept running.

grounded_facts: Drew Ellison and Quinn Hayes face off in the Fairview Motel atrium, immediately engaging in combat with bladed weapons after locking eyes.
memories.memory_text: I locked eyes with Quinn Hayes in the Fairview Motel atrium, and we both raised our bladed weapons, ready to fight as the lights shattered around us.

grounded_facts: Quinn Hayes lunges at Drew Ellison with a hiss, initiating physical combat with bladed weapons.
memories.memory_text: I saw Quinn Hayes lunge at me with a hiss, and our blades clashed immediately as he attacked.

grounded_facts: Quinn Hayes engages Drew Ellison in brutal combat, overpowering him with physical force and biting into his stomach.
memories.memory_text: I fought Quinn Hayes with my sword, but he overpowered me, ripping into me with his hands and then biting into my stomach—I screamed and hit his head with everything I had, but he wouldn't let go.

grounded_facts: A brutal sword fight between Quinn Hayes and Drew Ellison escalates into hand-to-hand combat resulting in mutual fatalities.

memories.memory_text: I was just a kid when I heard Harborview Station was lost... I remember lying in bed, dreaming I'd be the one chosen to go.
I woke up gasping, couldn't scream—my body jerking, tearing the mask off, light flickering through the glass as I came back.
I saw the tattoo on my arm—FLT>>005»015—while wiping the grime off with a towel. Didn't mean anything to me, not then.
There was a photo tucked in the locker door—some woman, smiling. I didn't know her. Checked the back—nothing. I put it in my pocket anyway.
I saw Skyler Ellison smiling at me while I knelt beside her, holding her hands—just for a second, then it was gone.
I heard thumps coming from a Lakeview House, then Parker York kicked his way out, gasping—I tried to help him up but he snapped at me to get the light out of his eyes.
I saw Parker York fumbling at the lockers, not recognizing his own name or that photo of his Jesse Nolan—he looked just as lost as I felt, like none of it meant anything to him anymore.
When he pulled on his uniform and shoved his feet into those boots, I caught a glimpse of his tattoo—faded, old—nothing like mine, which looked fresh, like it was inked yesterday.
I told Parker York I could take it — the shaft, the tight space, the risk — and that he could guide me over two-way, like it was nothing, even though my jaw was clenched so hard it ached.
I pointed at the Wesley Hawthorne's pod and asked how long he waited, voice tight, because the lights flickered and the red key shuddered — like it was dying, like we were already too late.

I squeezed into the shaft, the metal walls pressing in, and started crawling forward on my stomach—grunt, slide, breath—each movement tight and slow, the pen-lamp clenched in my teeth as Parker York's light faded behind me.

I saw a spider—real, moving—dropped on a thread, then scurried off. That meant life, movement, something still alive in this dead the red key. I took a left, following it. Made sure Parker York noted it.
I couldn't breathe in that shaft—walls closing in, sweat blinding me, pipes squeezing the space smaller. I screamed into the dark, 'I just want OUT of this FUCKING THING!'

I remember laughing with Parker York over his stupid dream about being naked at the Rose Bowl—something about two years looking for clothes. It broke the tension, and for a second, I could breathe again.
I pulled out Skyler Ellison's photo, shining my light on her face, and it hit me—eight years. I left her, and I don't even remember saying goodbye. That can't be right.
I saw bolts, torn fabric, and blood on the walls—someone else had made it through here before me, and I wasn't alone.
I felt my sweat roll forward, realized the shaft was sloped, and then I started sliding—couldn't stop, lost the light, crashed headfirst into a grate.
I stabbed the envelope opener into the vent just as the light broke through—metal bent under my hand, and I slammed my elbow into it again and again, BANG, BANG, until it gave way.
I pulled myself out of that overhead compartment, every muscle screaming—got to my feet, called Parker York, tried the transmitter, but all I got was static.
I jammed the pipe into the gap and forced the hatch open—it burst with a loud THUD, hydraulics hissing, and I stepped out slow, gun up, not knowing what was out there.
I remember Parker York saying there's no rescue, no turning around—that this the red key wasn't built to return. The way he said it, like he was remembering something terrible, made my stomach drop.
He looked at the Lakeview House and said we're not crew—we're the cargo. I felt like the floor gave out. That's all he said before his voice just... trailed off.
I'm a settler... this the red key was never going back. Redwood Industries—it was a one-way ticket. I finally understood what we were really doing here.
I saw her—Skyler Ellison—sleeping. I was leaning close, just watching her. I loved her... how could I have left her?
I told Parker York over the radio — they're here, somewhere on board. I could hear my own voice tighten as I said it, like the truth was clawing its way out.

I saw Riley Foster behind that Lakeview House, mouthing 'Don't follow me! I can't help you—' right before the wire snapped around his neck. I tried to crank the the glass notebook, but it jammed when I needed it most.

I fired at Quinn Hayes through the glass, but the blast just shattered against it—useless. He stepped forward, unharmed, his skin slick with fluid, eyes hidden, and then the Elliot Everett came for me.
I grabbed Drew Ellison's shoulder hard—he was going to bolt and get us all killed. We couldn't move, not with those things coming.
I saw the ID tattoo on Riley Arden's hand—BIO-T>>218>>076—right when she opened the vault door. The light flickered, but I saw it clear.

I walked up to that wall of glass tubes, all fogged with condensation, and couldn't believe what I was seeing—labels for mountain goats, octopi, every kind of animal... this whole vault was meant to repopulate a planet.

I stared at the screen showing Tanis, the planet we were supposed to reach, and whispered the name—Tanis—and then Riley Arden said I couldn't remember... like I should've known all along how long we'd been asleep.
I saw hundreds of Lakeview House, all stacked up and empty—hatches open, no one inside. I couldn't believe it... they were all gone.
I remembered my Jesse Nolan might be on this the red key—she wasn't crew, but spouses were brought along. I had to check the pods, even if Riley Arden said she wouldn't be here.
I screamed at Jesse Colter to shut off the gas after he trapped us and flooded the tank—my throat burned, I could barely breathe, but I kept the the glass notebook raised and aimed right at him.
When he asked to trade after shutting off the gas, I kept the barrel trained on him—his grin didn't fool me, not after he tried to kill us with that vapor.

I heard it—static at first, then words forming. Jesse Colter cranked the playback, and it got clearer: 'You are all that's left of us. Good luck, God bless... and God's speed.' I stood closer, trying to take it in.
The Pinecrest Warehouse's gone into the final cycle—I felt it in the shudder, saw the fear on their faces. I told them we're done, and I meant it.

The Pinecrest Warehouse's in its final rotation—I told Parker York we're running out of time, the whole the red key's heading into permanent shutdown and there'll be no return. I could hear my own voice crack through the radio, desperate for him to understand.

relations.relation_summary: The relationship between Owen Quincy and the Elliot Everett is defined by intense hostility and survival-driven conflict. Social relationship evidence consistently portrays the Elliot Everett as active threats to Owen Quincy, who is repeatedly fleeing, evading, and defending himself against their attacks. The Elliot Everett pursue Owen Quincy with clear intent to capture or kill, surrounding him, targeting him with weapons, and reacting aggressively to his presence, indicating they view him as prey or an enemy. This adversarial dynamic is reinforced by Owen Quincy’s own actions—he resists their attacks, uses weapons against them, and intervenes to protect others from their violence. The common events confirm this antagonism through direct physical confrontations: Owen Quincy charges into a Nico Adler and initiates a brutal fight, and later participates in a group attack that subdues a Nico Adler. These violent encounters underscore a relationship rooted in survival, fear, and mutual aggression. There is no evidence of alliance, communication, or evolution toward cooperation; the relationship remains consistently hostile throughout. The emotional dynamic is one of terror and resistance, shaping Owen Quincy’s decisions to remain vigilant, avoid detection, and fight back when cornered. The evidence is insufficient to confirm any underlying motive for the Elliot Everett’ behavior beyond predation or territorial hostility.

The relationship between Owen Quincy and Skyler Ellison is defined by a deep romantic and emotional connection, strongly indicative of a spousal bond. Social relationship evidence highlights Owen Quincy's enduring love and emotional attachment, as seen in a flashback where he watches Skyler Ellison sleep with profound affection, and his distress over a photo of her suggests she is someone he once lived with intimately. The kinship_with/spouse label is further supported by Owen Quincy’s anguished questioning about why he left her and his inability to recall saying goodbye, which implies a significant and painful separation. This emotional turmoil is reinforced through common events, particularly the memory of Owen Quincy kneeling beside Skyler Ellison—a gesture of intimacy and vulnerability that resurfaces during a moment of psychological conflict. memories.memory_text: I heard something—movement near the galley. I turned fast, saw a man peeking, and I hit him before he could. Blood sprayed when I clocked him with the opener, he went down hard. I kept the blade to his throat and made sure he stayed still.

I patted him down fast—tools first, then his shoes. His radio crackled, a voice calling his name. I didn't recognize it. I didn't care. I needed those shoes. But that voice… something about it made me tense. I didn't stay to find out why.

I lunged from the cabinet and drove my knife at the man’s neck—he tasted the bar, thought it was safe, but I couldn’t let him get the upper hand. His grip was strong, stopping the blade just in time, but I had the drop on him.

After the shot rang out and they backed away, I stayed low, knife still in hand, watching them retreat. Owen Quincy and the other one—Drew Ellison—left together, and I didn’t move, just watched from the shadows, trying to figure out if they were really gone or setting a trap.
I pressed my palm to the scanner just as the power surge hit—felt the panel come alive under my hand, then the hydraulics groaned and the door started to open.
I saw Owen Quincy glance at my arm when the light hit—it flashed across the tattoo, BIO-T>>218>>076—didn't say anything, but I know he saw it.
I jammed the pipe into the door handles after locking it—my way of making sure nothing gets in. I’ve learned not to trust flimsy locks, not after everything I’ve seen.
I dumped my bag’s contents onto the pile of scavenged things—another day, another haul. This place has become more home than the rest of the red key ever was.
I told Owen Quincy I wasn't waiting—if he wanted to stay, he could find his own way. I had to keep moving. We couldn't afford to stop, not with him hunting.
I heard the crunch behind me, then Owen Quincy froze—something white in the dirt. I turned just as he realized it was a finger bone. No time. I had to keep going.

I pulled Owen Quincy back when he tried to stand—there was no time to play hero, not with footsteps closing in. I knew we had to move, so I found the grate and got us into the shaft before the Elliot Everett finished their... feast.
I was trying to get us out of there alive—Owen Quincy didn’t get it, none of them did. I could see the doubt in his eyes, like I’d led us in circles on purpose.
I didn’t need to help him at all. If it weren’t for me, he’d still be stuck on level eight with the Hong-Kong Express, playing games instead of surviving.
I heard it—the message from Earth—finally clear after all that noise. 'You are all that's left of us.' I felt my breath catch, like the air had been pulled out of the room.
I saw the drawings on the wall—pilots turning on each other, blood, pieces missing. Jesse Colter kept saying 'chop, chop, chop' like it was a game, and then: only one left. Spencer Huxley.
I woke up choking, heart slamming—Jesse Colter was right over me, sniffing my body like I was meat. I thought he was going to eat me.
Owen Quincy just sat there, giving up, saying it was over. I grabbed him—screamed in his face not to give up on me. I couldn't let him quit.
I saw the Sasha Sinclair move like one of them, too fast, too sure—it wasn't human. My voice came out raw, like something ripped loose: 'My God. They're... breeding.'

I remember the blue glow moving past the doorway, those silhouettes—too many Elliot Everett—and Jesse Colter saying we should turn back. I told him there’s nowhere to go, we can’t give up, not after coming this far.

I saw Owen Quincy freeze when he saw the empty Lakeview House covered in blood. He was holding Skyler Ellison's photo, and I asked if he thought she was on the red key. He said she wasn't here and wouldn't have come with him.
I told him she saved his life by not coming. He frowned, then slowly nodded. He looked at the nameplate Jesse Nolan and said 'Jesse Nolan.' I asked if he knew her.
I told Jesse Colter to shut up and move—he was frozen, blocking the way while we were exposed on the catwalk. I couldn't let his fear get us killed.
I watched the Elliot Everett shift in their sleep as the crank's whine rose—their bodies twitching, limbs tensing—and I held my breath, waiting to see if one would open its eyes.

I saw them all wake up—every Nico Adler on that floor—turning their heads at once, staring right at us. I couldn't move, just felt the cold hit my chest, then I heard Drew Ellison slam his the glass notebook and I snapped—'Hurry! Go!'

I grabbed Owen Quincy's shoulder, voice cracking—'Owen Quincy!'—as the Elliot Everett closed in, Harper Foster cackling like it was over, and then the steam exploded from the valves, fire bursting out, blinding us, shaking the whole the red key.
The lights flashed on all at once—blinding, everywhere—and the floor lit up like it was alive, forcing us to run before we could even understand what was happening.

I ran with Owen Quincy along the top of the Lakeview House wall, thirty feet above the fighting—passengers and Elliot Everett tearing into each other below. Lights flashed like a nightmare, bursting, sparking, everything chaos.
I screamed at Jesse Colter as he slammed the hatch shut—'You snake bastard—OPEN IT!'—but he just locked us out, leaving Owen Quincy and me running while the Elliot Everett gained on us.
What's happened... to us? Where are we? I said it out loud, staring at those black-coated windows that looked like space but weren't—no stars, just dust, floating like something was wrong.

I stepped toward the window, trying to see through the fungus, and then—suddenly—jumped back. A figure was sitting in the chair. Spencer Huxley. Just... there. Motionless. Staring. I didn't see him come in. Didn't hear anything.

I was fighting the current, trying to stay out of that chamber, but Owen Quincy grabbed me and yanked me inside—'NO!? Are you crazy—'—then he shouted 'GET IN!' and slammed the hatch as water roared in.
I fought him—Owen Quincy—when he tried to shove that mask on me. I couldn't breathe, the water was rising, and I kept gasping, 'No! I can't—Not like this!'
The mask was on me, I could feel the air pushing in, heavy and thick—my eyes wouldn't stay open. The light through the porthole got brighter, white and warm, just before everything went dark.
I gasped for air, my eyes flickering open, sunlight burning into my skull—I didn’t know where I was. All I could choke out was, 'Where are we? What happened?'

memories.memory_text: I woke up gasping, heart pounding, the cold floor beneath me as someone shone a light in my face—I didn’t know who they were, didn’t recognize the name 'Owen Quincy'—and all I could do was demand, 'Who are you?' and then, 'Where... are we?'
I cranked the auxiliary power handle hard, feeling the resistance as the magnetos whined, and finally saw the panel lights flicker to life with a dim glow.
After getting the comms online, I keyed the mic and announced my name and team—'Parker York of Eastwood Department'—into the dead static, scanning the Lakeview House as I waited for any response.

I couldn't bring myself to enter that narrow shaft—just the thought of being trapped in such a tight space made my chest close up, and I had to tell Owen Quincy the truth: I can't do it, not even for this mission.

I saw the photo slip out of Owen Quincy’s pocket when he tucked that envelope opener away—something about a woman, a wedding. I asked if she was his Jesse Nolan, and he said 'Yeah... I think so.' That answer stuck with me—how could you not know?

Then it hit me—his face, that argument on the flight. I remembered him pushing for the window seat, all smug, and me refusing to let him have it. I called him a cocky little shit, and he shot back that I was a cranky old bastard.

I saw the emblem above the name plate—Redwood Industries—and for a second, something in my head shifted, like a door cracking open. The spiral on the globe felt familiar, too familiar, and then my frown tightened before I even realized I was reacting.

The thumping came—THUMP... SCRAPE... THUMP—and I snapped out of it, swinging my flashlight toward the wall. I panned it up slowly, then across the ceiling, my body tense, feeling the weight of being alone in that room.
I told Owen Quincy I got the door open—just to get him to stop panicking, to give him something else to focus on, even if it wasn't true.

I told Owen Quincy I was kidding to snap him out of his panic—he needed to laugh, just for a second, so he wouldn’t spiral. Then I told him to breathe, easy, like we were going to get through this together.

I remembered the dream—naked at the Rose Bowl, everyone drunk but me, two years looking for clothes. When Owen Quincy repeated 'two years,' something clicked: our duty rotation, Eastwood Department… and then he said it—eight years.
I remember staring at the red key's emblem and realizing this wasn't some routine mission—none of us were here by accident. This flight was a select pick, something deliberate.
I rubbed my hand over the steel emblem, brushing away dust. My fingertips trembled as I paused, frowning.
I remember being interviewed, my voice steady despite the weight of it—my mother seeing me on the news, pride in her eyes. We weren’t just pilots… we were heroes.
I called out to Owen Quincy over the radio, shouting into the silence, desperate for any response as he struggled in that shaft.
I heard a pop of static over the speaker, and then I called out—'Owen Quincy...? You alright? Owen Quincy!?'—my voice rising because something felt wrong.
I kept flipping through the radio channels, calling for Owen Quincy, my voice tight—'Com'on, man. You there?'—but all I got was silence and that damn scrape-thump sound getting closer.

I snapped the handle off a storage bin and backed toward the Lakeview House, gripping it like a bat, my fingers trembling as I kept switching channels and staring at the wall where the scraping was coming from.
I ran my hand over the doors—deep scrapes and dents covered them, like someone had fought to get out or in. No one sealed the chamber, no emergency lockdown… that meant no one was coming to save us.

I looked at the scattered tools and the torn-open vent, then at the Lakeview House—something clicked. This wasn't a regular transport. We weren't hauling cargo… we *were* the cargo. the red key was never meant to come back.
Owen Quincy suddenly demanded, 'Where is your Jesse Nolan?' and I could only say 'What?'—his intensity caught me off guard, like he’d uncovered something I wasn’t ready to face.
I remember now—there are non-crew on this the red key. Not just crew. Passengers. Spouses. Hidden somewhere in the dark. The thought hits me like a cold pulse, and I can't shake the unease.

I told Owen Quincy we had to focus on taking control of the red key first—finding anyone else wouldn’t matter if we couldn’t stop whatever was happening. I needed him to understand that saving the red key was the only way to save them all.
I heard Owen Quincy was disoriented, so I told him to check the hatch marker over the door to figure out his location—I could guide him if he gave me a reference point.
I heard Owen Quincy's voice over the radio suggesting he could reset the Pinecrest Warehouse, and I asked him if he really knew how—because that was the only thing that mattered in that moment.

I shut down Owen Quincy’s theory about Pandorum—Harborview Station was a mechanical failure, nothing more. I had to keep the story straight, even if he kept pushing with those questions about rotation shifts and overrides.
I told Owen Quincy not to look back—just to keep moving—because stopping meant death, and I couldn't let him freeze when the Elliot Everett were on him.
I found the tattoo on Spencer Huxley's arm—FLT>>004>>012—and it hit me: he's not a successor, he's from Flight Team Four. That means he was supposed to wake before me, not after.
When I asked him about coming from the bridge and not knowing our location, he got tense and evasive—like he was hiding something, or couldn't remember. That didn't fit a commanding officer.
I remember asking if Earth was really gone, and when Spencer Huxley said it was wiped away, I couldn't process it—just sat back, shaking my head, whispering 'Oh my God...'
I stared at the screen—Earth wasn't there. I kept scanning, but it was gone. How could they have let this happen?

I heard Owen Quincy's voice over the radio saying the Pinecrest Warehouse was in its final stage, the red key dying, everything heading into permanent shutdown—I felt the weight of it as Spencer Huxley just stood there, watching me, saying nothing.
I tore open the control panel and started pulling wires, trying to hot-wire the sealed door—direct channels were fried, and the only way to restore access was a manual patch.
Spencer Huxley kept pacing and questioning me, doubting the Sasha Sinclair could save the red key, but I kept working and said he's our only shot—I had to hold onto that, even if I couldn't look up.
